features.name: Linux desktop
features.detail: Debian/RPM binaries, Arch packaging and Ubuntu PPA are documented; binary Python compatibility is release-specific.

features.name: Scan originals in place
features.detail: Add existing folders to the scan list; no managed photo import is required.

features.name: Multi-folder scans
features.detail: Add multiple recent/new folders or drag directories into the selection list before a single scan.

features.name: Exact content duplicate scan
features.detail: Standard Contents groups by file size, drops unique-size files and compares MD5 digests. This is hash-based equality, not documented full byte-for-byte verification.

features.name: Word-based filename similarity
features.detail: Normalize case/punctuation and compare shared words against filter hardness; optional character-weighting and approximate-word matching increase flexibility, time and false positives.

features.name: Ordered or reordered filename fields
features.detail: Dash-separated fields are compared individually; an order-independent mode can match artist/title reversed between files, with each field used once.

features.name: Music-tag duplicate matching
features.detail: Music mode compares chosen tags such as artist/title as separate fields and displays audio metadata columns. This is not a claim of acoustic fingerprinting.

features.name: Perceptual picture matching
features.detail: Picture Contents averages RGB values over a 15×15 grid and compares corresponding cells against a configurable threshold; 100 applies an additional exact-picture constraint, while 99 permits small differences.

features.name: Cross-resolution and rotated picture matches
features.detail: Preferences can permit differing dimensions and rotations in the same picture duplicate group and allow mixed file extensions.

features.name: EXIF timestamp candidate matching
features.detail: A separate scan treats matching DateTimeOriginal tags as duplicate candidates; modified images retaining the timestamp can be false positives.

features.name: Recursive duplicate folder detection
features.detail: Folder Contents compares contained file contents recursively and returns the largest matching folders instead of redundantly listing their matching subfolders.

features.name: Cached picture analysis
features.detail: Time-consuming 15×15 picture-analysis results are cached in a database. The release also refers to a standard-content hashing cache bug fix.

features.name: Multi-core picture comparison
features.detail: Picture matching is documented as utilizing multiple cores, while still requiring quadratic pair comparisons; no benchmark was performed.

features.name: Protected reference directories
features.detail: Reference-state folders cannot contribute deletable duplicates. States inherit to subfolders unless overridden, and protected references cannot be demoted.

features.name: Excluded directory states
features.detail: Exclude roots or individual subfolders from scanning with inherited per-folder state.

features.name: Manual and rule-driven keeper selection
features.detail: Defaults to a protected reference or largest file; manually promote a duplicate or apply ordered size/folder/filename and other prioritization criteria with tie-breakers.

features.name: Delete every group member
features.detail: Group references cannot be marked, ensuring at least one group member remains; reference-folder members are additionally protected.

features.name: Persistent ignored match pairs
features.detail: Add Selected to Ignore List suppresses that duplicate/reference pair in future scans, not the file globally; the same file may match a different reference. Ignore list can be cleared.

features.name: Discard candidates without changing files
features.detail: Remove selected/marked candidates from results or leave them unmarked; removing result rows does not touch their files.

features.name: Reference-versus-duplicate details
features.detail: Details panel compares selected file and reference metadata; numeric Delta Values show relative differences and differing text is highlighted. This evidence establishes metadata comparison, not a thumbnail comparison claim.

features.name: Dupes-only review mode
features.detail: Hide reference rows to sort all duplicate files independently by columns, combine with relative values, and mark batches such as extension or bitrate differences.

features.name: Post-scan wildcard or regex filtering
features.detail: Case-insensitive filter searches complete paths using simple text plus wildcard or regular expressions. Nonmatching members remain visible but cannot be marked through the filtered view.

features.name: Keyboard batch marking
features.detail: Shift/Control/Command selection and Space toggle selected duplicate marks; marked and selected states remain distinct.

features.name: XHTML result export
features.detail: Exports current result columns into an XHTML report and opens it in the browser.

features.name: Trash by default
features.detail: Send Marked to Trash uses the OS trash; a separate direct-delete option bypasses it for cases such as incompatible NAS deletion.

features.name: Review and deletion options
features.detail: Scanning first produces reviewable groups; deletion presents options. Groups discard ambiguous non-transitive matches rather than overlapping candidates that might delete distinct files.

features.name: Replace deletions with hard links
features.detail: Deletion options can link removed paths to reference files; manual documents macOS/Linux support and Windows version/admin-privilege caveats.

features.name: Replace deletions with symbolic links
features.detail: Alternative link replacement uses symlinks, with the explicit caveat that moving/deleting their reference target breaks them.

features.name: Ignore existing inode aliases
features.detail: macOS/Linux preference excludes duplicate candidates already referring to the same inode.

features.name: Move or copy marked candidates
features.detail: Destination layout can be flat or recreate relative/absolute source paths; source folders can be removed after becoming empty.

features.name: Collision-safe copy/move names
features.detail: Copy/move naming conflicts prepend a number instead of silently overwriting the destination filename.

features.name: Rename selected file
features.detail: Action menu prompts for a new filename; a batch naming-template system is not established by this action.

features.name: Custom external comparison commands
features.detail: Configure a command with duplicate and reference path placeholders; results can also open in the default application or reveal their containing directory.

limitations.text: Picture comparisons are quadratic and CPU-intensive. Similar-word matching increases false positives; EXIF timestamp identity alone can match edited variants. These candidate modes need review.
MD5 content matching is not cryptographic proof against deliberately forged files, and no byte-by-byte verification is established in the inspected scan manual.
4.2.0–4.3.0 standard-content scans could falsely identify nonduplicates when hashing cache errors occurred; 4.3.1 adds error handling and guards for nonempty files without digests.
All-copy removal is intentionally disallowed. Link and trash behavior depends on platform and filesystem; direct delete bypasses recoverable OS trash.
The inspected manuals do not establish photo-library albums, face recognition, maps, video similarity, an operation journal, encrypted storage or a general media playback engine.

gaps: No claim of current GUI visual-thumbnail comparison from the inspected metadata-details manual.
Some platform details in pinned help are historical; release-specific packaging is distinguished.

R07.summary: Cross-platform local file catalogue built around relational, inheritable tags and typed metadata fields, layered over an existing directory without mandatory file copies or per-file sidecars.
deployment: Windows, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon and Linux desktop builds
Portable Windows and Linux distributions; official releases on GitHub
Optional FFmpeg for video/audio and ripgrep for faster scanning
R07.storage_model: One content-root directory per library, including subfolders. A .TagStudio directory holds ts_library.sqlite, thumbnail cache, ignore rules and database backups. Entries store relative paths, so the complete root is portable. Multiple separately opened libraries have independent tags; concurrent users on one library are unsupported.
R07.privacy_model: Local catalogue does not alter source files except explicit operations such as Move to Trash; no cloud upload required. Network/NAS or cloud-mounted folders can be used via the OS. Native cloud and nonlocal LLM integration are explicitly outside the project's scope; this is not encrypted-vault storage.
maturity_notes: Manifest latest release Alpha v9.6.4 (2026-10-02); inspected main 246f162a70b67203ca4d8a425b0ba4c61cf25468.
README retains v9.5-era statements contradicted by newer manuals/roadmap: custom field templates/names and substring smartcase path search are documented now.
Roadmap marks Fix Duplicate Files as a regression despite the older macros page describing a dupeGuru import tool; that capability is not counted present.
v10 denotes intended feature completeness; 9.x does not mean a mature final release.

features.name: Native Windows desktop builds
features.detail: README explicitly provides official executable Windows builds from GitHub Releases; these are desktop applications, not a Docker-host or browser-only compatibility claim.

features.name: Native Intel and Apple Silicon macOS builds
features.detail: README explicitly lists macOS desktop builds for both Intel and Apple Silicon, distributed through official GitHub Releases.

features.name: Native Linux desktop builds
features.detail: README explicitly lists executable Linux desktop releases; it warns that package-manager distributions are unofficial rather than claiming official support for every package source.

features.name: Portable Windows and Linux releases
features.detail: README explicitly offers self-contained portable Windows and Linux releases intended to be easier to move between locations; macOS portable packaging is not claimed.

features.name: Translated desktop interface
features.detail: Roadmap marks interface translations and application language settings implemented; v9.6.4 specifically updates Dutch, French and Hungarian translations. This does not imply the separately planned multilingual tag-name feature.

features.name: Sort catalogue results by filename
features.detail: Roadmap explicitly marks filename result sorting completed in v9.5.2; file creation/modification/capture-date sorting remains unchecked and is not included in this claim.

features.name: Sort by catalogue addition date
features.detail: Results can be ordered by when the file entry was added to the library, explicitly distinct from file creation, modification or photo capture time.

features.name: Shuffle result ordering
features.detail: Random/Shuffle Sort is explicitly checked as implemented in the current search-result sorting roadmap.

features.name: Catalogue files in place
features.detail: Creates a layer over a chosen directory and its descendants without moving, copying or changing media files.

features.name: Independent selectable libraries
features.detail: Open/Create selects a library root; each library has its own tags, fields, colors and database, not a global tag universe.

features.name: Portable library root
features.detail: Relative entry paths allow moving the whole content/data folder together, including external drives or differently mounted NAS paths.

features.name: Refresh new/modified files
features.detail: Manual Refresh Directories and configurable scan-on-open update the catalogue. README mentions a 10,000-file threshold, while newer manual describes a user toggle; exact threshold behavior is not independently resolved.

features.name: Gitignore-like scan exclusions
features.detail: .ts_ignore supports directory-relative patterns, *, ?, **, ranges, comments and negation. Applies when adding new files, not retroactively; cannot re-include children of an excluded parent.

features.name: Repair moved/unlinked entries
features.detail: Tool finds missing entries, searches/relinks or removes only catalogue records after confirmation. README says matching uses filenames, ignores ambiguous matches and cannot relink renamed files.

features.name: Rich tag objects
features.detail: Tags have nonunique unrestricted names, shorthand, aliases, colors and relationships rather than just flat text labels.

features.name: Multi-parent tag inheritance
features.detail: Tags inherit from multiple parents transitively; searching a parent finds entries assigned descendants without redundantly adding every ancestor to each file.

features.name: Aliases and contextual names
features.detail: Aliases/shorthand are searchable; marked parent tags add their name or shorthand in display parentheses to distinguish same-named tags without changing base identity.

features.name: Tag-driven inspector categories
features.detail: Category tags group inheriting tags in inspector, including multiple categories. Per-tag exclusions control category display; v9.6.4 release confirms the feature.

features.name: Custom tag palettes
features.detail: Built-in and user-defined namespaced palettes set primary/secondary text/border colors on tags; not an independently established media color-label rating system.

features.name: Customizable Favorite tag
features.detail: Built-in Favorite and Archived tags inherit Meta Tags; their category/parent behavior can be customized.

features.name: Hidden-tag archive filtering
features.detail: Is Hidden excludes tagged entries from default searches; Archived carries it by default and a checkbox includes hidden entries.

features.name: Custom typed field templates
features.detail: Create/edit/delete custom templates for text or datetime fields. Template information is copied into an entry; editing the entry does not mutate the template. Newer manual/roadmap supersede README's fixed-name claim.

features.name: Text and datetime annotations
features.detail: Single-line/multiline text stores titles, notes or comments; datetime values follow application date format. Values are in the catalogue, not written to media.

features.name: Tag multiple selected entries
features.detail: Add Tags to Selected supports fast keyboard searching/creation and repeated Enter-to-add; unassigned tags are removable in inspector.

features.name: Convert folder hierarchy to tag inheritance
features.detail: Macro previews a hierarchy for confirmation, creates a tag per folder, applies to entries and assigns parent-folder tags as parents; v9.6.4 fixes this workflow.

features.name: Alias-aware inherited tag search
features.detail: Default search matches tag names, shorthand and aliases including inherited parents; tag: is optional.

features.name: Boolean and nested queries
features.detail: Implicit/explicit AND, OR, NOT and parentheses; quotes or underscore substitution escape multiword names.

features.name: Substring/glob smartcase paths
features.detail: path: searches whole-path substrings by default or optional glob patterns; lowercase is case-insensitive, mixed case is sensitive. No forced case-sensitive all-lowercase query is available.

features.name: Extension/media-category filters
features.detail: filetype: and mediatype: search extensions or media classes; roadmap marks optional extension-synonym consolidation implemented.

features.name: Find untagged entries
features.detail: special:untagged finds entries without tags. special:empty availability conflicts across docs and is not included in this present claim.

features.name: Thumbnail grid and inspector
features.detail: Grid entries show detailed preview, file statistics, tags and fields in an inspector; roadmap marks infinite scrolling and configurable page size implemented.

features.name: Tagging and library shortcuts
features.detail: Shortcuts cover opening/refreshing libraries, creating/managing tags, adding to selected entries and saving backups, with macOS equivalents.

features.name: Video thumbnails/player
features.detail: Requires FFmpeg; thumbnails use a viable middle frame. Player supports play/pause, loop, autoplay, volume/mute and timeline scrubber, not yet fullscreen per roadmap.

features.name: Audio playback and waveform preview
features.detail: FFmpeg enables common audio formats. Thumbnails use cover art or waveform; waveform caching is explicitly not implemented.

features.name: Camera RAW previews
features.detail: Matrix lists Canon CRW/CR2/CR3, DNG, Fuji RAF, Nikon NEF/NRW, Olympus ORF, Panasonic RAW/RW2 and Sony ARW.

features.name: HEIF/HEIC previews
features.detail: HEIF and HEIC are explicitly listed in image preview matrix.

features.name: AVIF previews
features.detail: AVIF appears in image support and in FFmpeg video-format listing; no universal animation support is inferred.

features.name: Static JPEG XL preview
features.detail: JXL is listed as supported image preview, but its animation column is explicitly unsupported.

features.name: Static vector preview
features.detail: SVG thumbnail/preview is supported; animation is explicitly not supported.

features.name: Animated image playback
features.detail: GIF, animated WebP and APNG play in Preview Panel; grid uses cached thumbnails.

features.name: PDF and office-document previews
features.detail: PDF previews render the first page. Apple iWork and OpenDocument documents use embedded thumbnails; PowerPoint support depends on an embedded thumbnail being available. This is preview support, not full document editing or established multipage navigation.

features.name: Creative-project thumbnail previews
features.detail: Photoshop PSD previews render a flattened image; Blender, Krita, Clip Studio Paint and other listed creative-project formats use embedded thumbnails, with availability caveats for formats such as Blender and Krita. Blender thumbnails do not establish interactive 3D model rendering.

features.name: Archive/eBook covers
features.detail: ZIP/RAR/7z/Tar variants show first archive image; EPUB shows cover and comic-book archives use cover/first page.

features.name: Font and plaintext previews
features.detail: Font formats show Aa/alphanumeric samples; plaintext previews render only first 256 bytes. Full text/syntax highlighting remain planned.

features.name: Explicit move to system trash
features.detail: README cites Move File(s) to Trash as the exception to otherwise non-modifying cataloguing; no general undo journal is asserted.

features.name: Autosave and timestamped database backups
features.detail: Library autosaves; manual Save Library Backup and automatic migration backups preserve ts_library.sqlite under backups. Original content files are excluded.

features.name: Library health/cleanup tools
features.detail: Library Information provides unlinked repair, remove ignored entries, delete old backups and remove legacy JSON without deleting source media.

features.name: Library information panel
features.detail: Panel shows library statistics and consolidated cleanup/backup access; no exact scale benchmark is claimed.

features.name: On-demand cached thumbnails
features.detail: Image thumbnails are generated first viewing or after modification and stored in .TagStudio/thumbs; full preview panel does not use them.

features.name: Optional fast directory scanner
features.detail: Installed ripgrep replaces wcmatch scanning for speed and Git-style glob parity; docs warn fallback pattern behavior can differ.

features.name: Experimental whole-library collage
features.detail: Tools manual describes a working early preview generating all-library collage output under .TagStudio/collages with no customization yet.

features.name: Legacy dupeGuru metadata mirroring
features.detail: Tools page describes loading dupeGuru result files and mirroring entry fields before deleting elsewhere, but current roadmap marks Fix Duplicate Files a regression still to restore; not a current built-in scanner.

features.name: Multiple roots per library
features.detail: Roadmap and library manual explicitly plan multiple content roots and a separately stored data directory; present root must host .TagStudio.

features.name: Composition relationships and overrides
features.detail: HAS/component relationships and tag overrides are planned, distinct from implemented parent inheritance.

features.name: Search custom field contents
features.detail: Field search and comparisons of date/duration/size/dimensions are unchecked roadmap tasks and explicitly unavailable in search manual.

features.name: OCR search roadmap
features.detail: OCR and fuzzy search appear as future low-priority roadmap items, not built-in recognition.

features.name: Nonexclusive nested entry groups
features.detail: Entry groups with nesting, per-group ordering, numbering and custom covers are planned; tags do not establish this album feature.

features.name: Separated core library/CLI
features.detail: UI-agnostic core and CLI with intended MIT licensing are roadmap work, not a released public API.

features.name: Event-driven automation macros
features.detail: Versioned TOML macros with add/refresh triggers and tag/field actions are planned; implemented Folders to Tags is a narrower tool.

features.name: Native cloud-service integration
features.detail: README explicitly rejects native cloud integration; OS-mounted virtual drives are suggested instead.

features.name: Native nonlocal LLM integration
features.detail: README explicitly rules out built-in ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/cloud-LLM connections; future external API possibilities do not change present status.

limitations.text: One library cannot be concurrently accessed by multiple users; multi-root and separately located library data remain planned.
Backups contain the catalogue SQLite file only, not original media; unlinked entries lose uncached stats and normal thumbnails.
README's relinker cannot handle renamed files and ignores multiple filename matches; automatic robust relinking remains roadmap work.
Ignore rules apply to new scans, not existing entries. FFmpeg is required for audio/video; waveform caching, full text preview and 3D rendering are not currently supported.

Duplicate-tool availability conflicts between older manual and regression roadmap; special:empty is advertised in README but marked unavailable for v9.5.0 in search manual. Neither is asserted currently working.
Face recognition, map browsing, perceptual matching, EXIF/XMP writing and media-content encryption were not established; tags for people/places are not AI recognition/geocoding.

gaps: Explicit documentation conflicts retained rather than resolved by assumptions.
No runtime preview/format tests; roadmap estimates are not release promises.

R08.summary: Cross-platform bulk uploader, migration, archive and stacking CLI for Immich, with detailed Google/iCloud/Picasa metadata reconstruction.
deployment: Standalone Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD binaries
CLI with interactive terminal status or headless mode
R08.storage_model: Reads folders, ZIP archives or remote Immich assets and uploads to an Immich server; archive mode instead writes ordinary year/year-month folders with original files, JSON metadata and preserved XMP sidecars. It is not a standalone browsable photo catalogue.
R08.privacy_model: Local sources can be organized into a local archive; uploads and server migrations transfer media and metadata to configured Immich API endpoints using API keys. Disabling TLS verification is offered but weakens transport verification. People names are imported metadata, not on-device face recognition.
maturity_notes: Frozen commit bc54ad2485b3e9c9b7c751445a28083950ffec60; latest release v0.32.0 (2026-06-25).
README warns this is an early, not extensively tested tool and recommends retaining backups.
v0.32.0 supports Immich V2/V3 and removes ReplaceAsset. Older upload reference still lists overwrite behavior; exact replacement semantics need version-specific verification.
Claim of handling 100,000+ photos is from the project, not an independent benchmark.

features.name: Windows command-line binary
features.detail: README documents a standalone Windows release binary without NodeJS or Docker; this is the uploader/archive CLI, not a native desktop gallery.

features.name: macOS command-line binary
features.detail: Standalone macOS executable distribution is documented for the upload/archive CLI; no desktop photo-browser UI is implied.

features.name: Linux command-line binary
features.detail: Standalone Linux executable is documented; connects to a separate Immich server for upload/server operations rather than providing its own gallery.

features.name: FreeBSD command-line binary
features.detail: README explicitly includes FreeBSD among the supported standalone executable platforms.

features.name: Folder and ZIP bulk uploads
features.detail: Uploads images/videos recursively from local directories or ZIP files with optional headless operation; no NodeJS or Docker installation is required for the CLI itself.

features.name: Google Takeout reconstruction
features.detail: Matches media with Google JSON and restores albums, descriptions, dates, locations and status flags. All split archive parts should be supplied together; unmatched media is excluded unless enabled.

features.name: Selective Takeout import
features.detail: Archived and partner photos default to included; trashed, unmatched and untitled-album inclusion are separate switches. Can select an album and group partner photos into a named album.

features.name: Import iCloud exports
features.detail: Reads iCloud export CSV metadata for dates and organization; optional --memories turns memories into albums. This is export ingestion, not documented live iCloud synchronization.

features.name: Reconstruct Picasa albums
features.detail: from-picasa automatically reads .picasa.ini, and folder ingestion can enable the same album-name processing.

features.name: Immich-to-Immich transfer
features.detail: Source and destination have separate server/API credentials and timeout/TLS settings; filters include dates, archived/trash state, favorites and minimum rating.

features.name: Archive media from all input sources
features.detail: archive supports folders/ZIPs, Google, iCloud, Picasa and Immich inputs, writing local media rather than requiring a destination server.

features.name: Chronological archive layout
features.detail: Writes year/year-month folders while retaining original filenames where possible; archive destination is not wiped before an update.

features.name: Incrementally update archives
features.detail: Adds new files, checks changed existing files and refreshes sidecars from current server state; archive operation does not propagate deletions.

features.name: Create albums from folders
features.detail: FOLDER or full PATH naming with customizable path joiner; alternatively put all media into one specified album or preserve Google/Picasa/iCloud associations.

features.name: Import and assign server tags
features.detail: Custom repeated tags, folder-derived tags, upload-session tags, Takeout timestamp tags and people-name tags are supported; imported people names do not establish face recognition.

features.name: Preserve hierarchical XMP keywords
features.detail: XMP is passed unchanged for Immich to consume hierarchical tags, descriptions, GPS, capture time/timezone and camera settings; actual interpretation is server-dependent.

features.name: Pair XMP sidecars for server ingestion
features.detail: Folder uploads process associated XMP unless --ignore-sidecar-files is enabled; originals are forwarded without modification.

features.name: Recover capture dates
features.detail: Technical guide prioritizes embedded EXIF, XMP, JSON and filename fallback, including common phone/screenshot naming patterns; this establishes ingestion metadata, not embedded rewriting of source files.

features.name: Export rich JSON metadata
features.detail: Archive sidecars contain original filename/date, GPS, album titles/descriptions, hierarchical tags, rating and favorite/archive/trash/partner flags; original XMP companions are also retained.

features.name: Manage RAW+JPEG companions
features.detail: Pairs same-basename assets using directory/time/size heuristics; can leave separate, keep only one type, or stack with RAW/JPEG chosen as cover. Existing-server keep-only modes delete the other type.

features.name: Manage HEIC+JPEG companions
features.detail: Offers separate, keep-HEIC, keep-JPEG and either-cover stacking modes based on matching basenames; this is not by itself proof of Live Photo video pairing.

features.name: Group photo bursts
features.detail: Uses device filename patterns for Huawei/Pixel/Samsung/Sony/Nexus/Nothing and a 900 ms temporal rule; modes include stack and RAW/JPEG preference. Docs warn rapid unrelated photos may be grouped.

features.name: Epson FastFoto front/back grouping
features.detail: Groups original, _a corrected and _b reverse-side scans with corrected image as stack cover.

features.name: Organize existing server assets
features.detail: stack operates on existing Immich assets without uploading media, using the same burst/pair/scanner rules and an optional timezone override.

features.name: Skip already uploaded assets
features.detail: Technical guide describes SHA-1 content checksums combined with server metadata and size checks to avoid redundant uploads; no perceptual similarity matching is established.

features.name: Preview upload or stack effects
features.detail: --dry-run simulates upload transfers or stack mutations; recommended before keep-only stack operations.

features.name: Skip unwanted files and folders
features.detail: --ban-file distinguishes directory patterns by trailing slash; defaults exclude NAS thumbnail trees, Lightroom catalogues, OS artifacts and iCloud Recently Deleted.

features.name: Filter ingestion by media type
features.detail: Include/exclude extensions and IMAGE/VIDEO/all filters constrain transfer/archive selection rather than providing a photo-browser search UI.

features.name: Filter transfer dates
features.detail: Accepts a year, year-month, day or explicit comma-separated date range; source-server transfer has a separate from-date-range option.

features.name: Resolve archive filename conflicts
features.detail: Archive output preserves names where possible, appends numbered suffixes on conflicts and sanitizes incompatible characters.

features.name: Restart interrupted uploads safely
features.detail: Deduplication lets a restarted command skip files already on the destination; this is restart/idempotence behavior, not a byte-level partial-transfer checkpoint claim.

features.name: Bound concurrent upload work
features.detail: Parallel tasks default from CPU count and can be set within 1–20; timeouts and stop/continue/tolerated-error policies are configurable.

features.name: Pause server processing during import
features.detail: --pause-immich-jobs defaults true to reduce thumbnail/other server workload during a bulk upload, requiring appropriate server permissions.

features.name: API traces and terminal progress
features.detail: Interactive terminal UI can be disabled; API tracing and log level/file controls support diagnosing upload and stacking operations.

features.name: Adapt to Immich V2/V3 APIs
features.detail: v0.32.0 detects server version and adapts errors/API behavior; album assets are retrieved through paginated metadata search for large collections.

features.name: Replace existing server media
features.detail: Upload manual lists --overwrite, but v0.32.0 removes ReplaceAsset and its permission; exact surviving replacement behavior is not established by these conflicting docs.

features.name: Standalone automation CLI
features.detail: Prebuilt cross-platform command-line program exposes upload, archive and stack operations without a NodeJS runtime.

limitations.text: Google .tgz archives are explicitly unsupported directly: extract first, and supply all Takeout roots together rather than their enclosing parent.
Upload/server stacking require a running Immich instance and adequately scoped API key; the CLI does not supply gallery browsing, ML recognition or sharing itself.
KeepRaw/KeepJPG/KeepHeic existing-server stack modes delete the alternate companion. Time-based bursts can group unrelated rapid shots; retain backups and preview.
Overwrite documentation conflicts with v0.32.0 API removal; not counted as present with clear semantics.

gaps: No standalone gallery/AI/map/share capabilities established; these belong to the separate Immich server.
Existing-asset overwrite semantics remain ambiguous after ReplaceAsset removal.
Actual decoder/rendering support follows Immich; importing a format does not prove local playback.

R09.summary: Federated photo/video social publishing server with chronological feeds, media posts, account controls and configurable federation/import features; not a private local photo catalogue.
deployment: Self-hosted PHP web application; Docker Compose recommended since September 2026
MySQL 8+ or MariaDB 11+ supported; PostgreSQL 14+ best-effort/not recommended
Browser/mobile-browser clients and OAuth/API integrations
R09.storage_model: Uploaded post media and account/post records are managed on the instance; optional object storage supports S3-compatible services and remote-media caches. Upload resizing/optimization means it should not be assumed to preserve archival originals.
R09.privacy_model: Instance operators host content and federation distributes eligible posts to other servers. Private accounts constrain visibility to approved followers but are not E2EE. Optional push gateway and video P2P tracker/STUN are additional external services. Hosting choices and administrator configuration materially affect privacy and availability.

features.name: Independent social instance
features.detail: Operators run their own PHP/database instance, with Docker Compose now recommended and conventional installation still supported.

features.name: Maintained Docker deployment
features.detail: README recommends maintained Docker images/Compose; stable release documents image rebuild and database migration workflow.

features.name: Desktop/mobile browser UI
features.detail: Help provides distinct desktop and mobile-browser post-composition entry points.

features.name: ActivityPub federation
features.detail: Instance-configured ActivityPub supports inbox/outbox/shared inbox and remote follows; network timeline can show other servers' content. The config flag defaults off, so federation depends on deployment.

features.name: Federated follower/block synchronization
features.detail: Configured federation supports signed follower-collection synchronization for followers-only delivery and block-list synchronization with cooldown/page limits.

features.name: Chronological social feeds
features.detail: Home shows followed accounts, Public shows local users and Network shows remote unmoderated content; these are chronological post feeds, not capture-date photo-library timelines.

features.name: Multi-image/video posts
features.detail: Composer accepts several media files together or individually; per-post count is instance-configured (default max_album_length is four).

features.name: Post captions
features.detail: Optional captions are attached during composition; maximum length is configured by the instance (500 default), rather than embedded IPTC writeback.

features.name: Per-media alternative descriptions
features.detail: Help documents media descriptions for visually impaired users, federated where supported. Help labels the composing UI experimental; current config sets an alt-text length limit of 1,000.

features.name: Composition photo filters
features.detail: Help describes choosing a filter in media options, labels it experimental and explicitly says filters are not federated.

features.name: Hashtag labeling
features.detail: Hashtags in captions/comments link to topic pages; help documents up to 30 hashtags per post/comment and public-post discoverability.

features.name: Hashtag search
features.detail: Search bar locates hashtags; public tagged posts can appear in discovery/search pages.

features.name: Subscribe to hashtag feeds
features.detail: Following a hashtag adds its photos/videos to feed; help gives follow limits of 20/hour and 100/day.

features.name: Approved-follower visibility
features.detail: Private Account setting limits photo/video visibility to approved followers and prompts about existing followers/new requests; not an encryption feature.

features.name: Unlisted publishing
features.detail: Unlisted posts do not appear in public timelines, as explicitly documented in timeline help.

features.name: Enable/disable replies per post
features.detail: Post menu can enable or disable comments/replies from desktop or mobile browser.

features.name: Account mentions
features.detail: Help documents tagging/mentioning up to five profiles in a post or comment; no automatic face recognition is implied.

features.name: Hide posts in archive
features.detail: Archived posts become unavailable for viewing/interactions and can be unarchived via profile Archives; help warns remote interactions may not be received while archived.

features.name: Private-message interface
features.detail: Direct supports photos/videos, text, feed posts, profiles, hashtags and locations; unsolicited messages may enter a filtered inbox. Help says direct media does not appear on hashtag/location pages or share onward through Pixelfed to other sites.

features.name: Mute/block/report controls
features.detail: Accounts can be muted/blocked from feeds; direct messages can be reported or deleted. Config bounds user mutes/blocks/domain blocks.

features.name: User keyword filters
features.detail: Current configuration supports custom content filters with bounded keywords, scan length, regex size and creation/update rates; default limits include 20 filters and 10 keywords per filter.

features.name: Restricted child accounts
features.detail: When administrators enable the feature, parents create linked child accounts and choose posting, commenting, liking/sharing and federation permissions; configured child-count limits apply.

features.name: Two-factor authentication
features.detail: Profile security help explicitly directs users to enable 2FA in security settings.

features.name: Account activity history
features.detail: Security help recommends reviewing Account Log for suspicious activity. This is account history, not a durable pre-operation crash-recovery file journal.

features.name: Follower/account migration
features.detail: Migration uses account aliases and compatible Pixelfed/Mastodon migration extensions. Post migration is documented for Pixelfed v0.11.9+ only when server-enabled; completion can take hours.

features.name: Instagram export import
features.detail: Imports Instagram JSON ZIP data including photos, captions and hashtags. Current dedicated config defaults to 1,000 posts, permits video/WebP, excludes archived posts and supports administrator/account-age/follower eligibility restrictions.

features.name: Embeddable profiles and posts
features.detail: Current instance configuration separately enables profile and post embeds by default; exact embed UI is not established by the unfinished help page.

features.name: Upload resizing and optimization
features.detail: Image optimization/resizing defaults on with configurable quality (80 default); upload file-size/account quotas are also configurable.

features.name: Video optimization
features.detail: Configuration documents video upload resizing/optimization enabled by default; accepted video MIME types remain instance-dependent.

features.name: HLS video streaming
features.detail: Optional HLS requires FFmpeg and defaults off; configurable bitrate governs generated streams.

features.name: Peer-assisted video distribution
features.detail: Optional P2P video requires HLS plus FFmpeg and defaults off; config identifies an external WebTorrent tracker and Google STUN server.

features.name: Cloud/object media storage
features.detail: Can store uploaded media on S3/Spaces/Rackspace-compatible backends and separately opt into caching remote federation media there; local media may be deleted after cloud upload.

features.name: Optional EXIF database storage
features.detail: MEDIA_EXIF_DATABASE defaults false; enabling stores EXIF in the database, without proving an end-user EXIF editing interface.

features.name: Developer API and OAuth
features.detail: README links official API documentation; config enables OAuth and application registration with rate limits, while personal access tokens are separately optional.

features.name: Atom syndication
features.detail: Federation configuration independently enables Atom feeds by default.

features.name: Optional push gateway
features.detail: Instance config supports the push.pixelfed.net gateway with an API key; notification garbage collection has separate configurable retention.

features.name: Instance registration policies
features.detail: Config controls open registration, email verification, maximum accounts and invites; curated registration and user invitations are optional modes.

features.name: Temporary account deactivation
features.detail: Disabling hides profile, photos, comments and likes until login reactivates the account; permanent deletion is separate and may have an admin-configured grace period.

features.name: Stories availability
features.detail: An off-by-default STORIES_ENABLED flag exists, but built-in Stories help is unfinished; inspected evidence does not establish lifecycle/privacy semantics or current shipped UI.

features.name: New Nuxt web UI
features.detail: v0.15.2 notes continued refactoring toward a new Nuxt interface, not a completed shipped replacement.

limitations.text: Username changes are explicitly unsupported in profile help; migration support varies by server/version and does not guarantee every post transfers.
Media formats, quotas, post size, import and federation are administrator-configured. Default MIME list contains JPEG/PNG/GIF even though video composition is documented.
Post filters are documented as experimental and not federated. Several help pages are unfinished, so feature completeness cannot be inferred from navigation labels.

Private visibility and direct messages are not evidence of E2EE. RAW archival handling, exact/perceptual duplicates, face recognition, maps, file-operation rollback and sidecar metadata are not established.

gaps: Official features web page returned no substantive body; pinned built-in help, configuration and release notes used instead.
Some help text appears legacy/experimental; stories and Nuxt replacement are not counted as present core features.
No live instance testing.

R10.summary: Image and general-file hosting frontend/backend with selectable external storage channels, public delivery, admin management and optional AI tagging.
deployment: Cloudflare Pages
Cloudflare Workers
Self-hosted Docker/Node.js/Hono service
Responsive web UI; separate ecosystem desktop/browser/blog clients
R10.storage_model: Metadata is decoupled from payloads: KV/D1 in Cloudflare deployments or SQLite/local data directory in Docker; payload channels include Telegram, Discord, R2, S3-compatible services, Hugging Face datasets and WebDAV. Direct links and CDN routes can bypass application-layer lifecycle controls.
R10.privacy_model: Self-hosting the service does not make storage or AI local. Files may be sent to selected providers; moderation and IP geolocation may contact additional services. Telemetry documentation warns that access links and domains may reach developers. AI keys are encrypted with an operator-managed secret, not media E2EE. Ordinary file reads usually need no authentication.

features.name: Operator-managed hosting
features.detail: Deploy the serverless service to one's Cloudflare account or self-host the Docker service; external storage providers remain separately configured.

features.name: Docker with SQLite
features.detail: Node.js/Hono Docker deployment uses SQLite and a persistent local data directory for service data.

features.name: Pages and Workers runtimes
features.detail: Cloudflare Pages and Workers run the shared engine with KV/D1 persistence; Workers deployment via GitHub Actions supports secret-typed variables.

features.name: Separate Satellite desktop companion
features.detail: README explicitly links MarSeventh/satellite as the project's desktop client, separately from the hosting server and web frontend. The inspected README does not establish exact supported desktop OSes or release parity, so no Windows/macOS/Linux availability is inferred.

features.name: Multiple upload entry methods
features.detail: Click, drag/drop, clipboard files or URLs and batch upload with live progress and retry.

features.name: Recursive folder upload
features.detail: Uploading folders preserves their relative directory structure; upload directory picker supports suggestions/completion.

features.name: Channel-aware large-file uploads
features.detail: Telegram/R2/S3/Discord support chunking, while Hugging Face uses LFS direct upload. Guide quotes Telegram 20 MB parts and Discord commonly 10/25 MB, subject to provider policy.

features.name: R2 and S3-compatible backends
features.detail: Configure R2 bindings or S3 endpoint, credentials, bucket, optional region/path-style/CDN and custom User-Agent; quota/cost varies by provider.

features.name: Telegram and Discord payload channels
features.detail: Store payloads through configured bots/channels, with optional proxy URLs and Discord Nitro setting; not private local disk storage.

features.name: Hugging Face dataset storage
features.detail: Configured token and dataset repository support private repositories and LFS-based large-file uploads.

features.name: Use a WebDAV storage provider
features.detail: Configure service URL, optional credentials/custom headers/public HTTP URL and automatic parent-directory creation.

features.name: Storage balancing and upload failover
features.detail: Manage multiple channel configurations, configure load balancing and automatically retry through another available channel after upload failure.

features.name: Browser-side image compression
features.detail: Optional upload optimization has configurable 1–20 MB trigger threshold and target size from 0.5 MB to that threshold; release excludes animated files to preserve animation.

features.name: Convert uploads to WebP
features.detail: Can convert images in-browser before uploading and displays conversion/size-reduction badges; animated GIF/WebP/APNG skip conversion.

features.name: Preserve animated uploads
features.detail: v2.7.8 skips local compression, WebP conversion and Telegram server-side compression for animated GIF, WebP and APNG.

features.name: Card and list file management
features.detail: Visual card/list views with rubber-band selection and batch operations in user-selected order.

features.name: Directory organization
features.detail: Create directories and navigate a visual directory tree; search can retain folders or recursively expand results, with preference saved.

features.name: Paged large-file listings
features.detail: File management uses paginated loading and mobile swipe pagination; this is not a claim of virtualized rows.

features.name: Light/dark and branding controls
features.detail: Theme switching, custom title/logo/icon/footer/link prefix and solid, fixed, rotating or Bing backgrounds are configurable; Bing is an external request option.

features.name: Video detail previews
features.detail: Release describes video preview loading/orientation handling in File Details; codec coverage is not exhaustively specified.

features.name: Audio preview player
features.detail: File Details provides a compact audio player and skeleton preview states; other file types fall back to an information row.

features.name: Search names and directories
features.detail: Feature guide lists name and directory search, with recursive expansion configurable in v2.7.8.

features.name: Search file tags
features.detail: Search/filter by user or AI-applied tags; no semantic embedding search is claimed.

features.name: File-type filtering
features.detail: Filter listed files by file type, using centralized MIME inference where metadata is missing or generic.

features.name: Channel and access-status filters
features.detail: Filter by storage channel and access state in addition to name/directory/tag/type.

features.name: Single and bulk tag editing
features.detail: Autocomplete and common tags assist editing; multiple selected files can receive tags, preserving existing ones when AI suggestions are added.

features.name: Hosting metadata display and editing
features.detail: Shows upload time, size and source IP; supports editing display filename/type and renaming File ID. These are hosting fields, not EXIF/IPTC editing.

features.name: Batch file organization
features.detail: Move files among directories with a visual destination picker; batch copy actions primarily concern generated links, so payload-copy semantics are not assumed.

features.name: Download hosted files
features.detail: File Details and batch management offer downloads; untransformed Read API returns original file content.

features.name: Direct hosting links
features.detail: Ordinary /file paths usually do not require authentication, subject to configured domain/file/moderation rules; links can use custom prefixes.

features.name: Copy URL, Markdown, HTML or BBCode
features.detail: Format preference is independent of content-link preference; choose hosted link or channel-specific Telegram/S3/CDN/WebDAV-public link, with unavailable choices falling back.

features.name: Visitor gallery for selected directories
features.detail: Enable unauthenticated browsing only for configured directory roots through /browse paths.

features.name: User and admin management
features.detail: Separate admin/user sessions, user upload controls and per-user upload statistics are documented; this does not establish isolated personal photo libraries.

features.name: Scoped API permissions and upload access
features.detail: API tokens independently grant upload/delete/list/manage, can expire and be auto-deleted; web/API uploads use configured authentication codes.

features.name: Hotlink and file-access controls
features.detail: Allowed source domains, file/IP allow/block lists and whitelist-only access can restrict public delivery; CDN caches may delay enforcement.

features.name: Password hashing and configurable sessions
features.detail: PBKDF2 with legacy password migration, HttpOnly sessions, isolated admin/user login and configurable age. HTTPS-only Secure cookies are configurable and disabled by default.

features.name: External or self-hosted content moderation
features.detail: Supports moderatecontent.com API or separately deployed nsfwjs service; moderatecontent free registration is noted unavailable.

features.name: Uploader IP recording and optional lookup
features.detail: Optional custom API receives upload IP and selected JSON fields populate UploadAddress. This is uploader network geolocation, not photo GPS mapping.

features.name: AI tag suggestions
features.detail: v2.7.8 provides manually invoked single/batch tag recognition with selectable suggestions, progress, cancellation of future work and failed-item retries, without needing stored thumbnails.

features.name: Configurable image-capable providers
features.detail: OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints, up to 8 providers/16 models, configurable prompts/language/preferred vocabulary and structured output; text connection test does not prove image capability.

features.name: Background automatic upload tagging
features.detail: Live documentation describes opt-in post-upload tagging of originals on supported channels, excluding External and images over 20 MiB. Disabled by default; upload response does not wait. Presence in frozen v2.7.8 is not established by its notes.

features.name: Encrypted provider-key storage
features.detail: AI_CONFIG_SECRET encrypts saved API keys; operator must keep a separate backup because secret loss/change makes keys unreadable. This does not encrypt hosted images end-to-end.

features.name: Delivery-time image sizing
features.detail: Read API accepts dimensions 1–4096, bounded aspect-preserving resize without enlargement, exact centre crop with cover or stretching with squeeze; admin can restrict allowed sizes.

features.name: URL-based centre crop
features.detail: With both dimensions and fit=cover, delivery resizes and centre-crops. It is not an interactive photo editor and requires image processing enabled.

features.name: Hosting REST API
features.detail: Upload/read/delete/batch-delete/list/random-image/token endpoints with CORS; reads support HEAD and channel-dependent byte ranges, but not Range combined with resizing.

features.name: Expose a WebDAV filesystem
features.detail: Enable /dav with separate credentials and destination channel for PROPFIND/GET/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS/MKCOL. Feature overview also lists MOVE, while dedicated method table omits it; MOVE compatibility needs verification.

features.name: External upload/client ecosystem
features.detail: README links browser, WordPress/Typecho/Obsidian/OpenList integrations; feature guide names PicGo. The separately named Satellite desktop client has its own deployment finding rather than being inferred from API availability.

features.name: Channel storage and upload statistics
features.detail: Counts, storage usage, channel distribution and date/channel upload trends, with capacity thresholds for R2/S3/WebDAV.

features.name: Batched index rebuilding
features.detail: Admin can rebuild the file index in batches to avoid runtime CPU limits.

features.name: Batch data backup and restore
features.detail: Feature guide documents batch file-data backup/restore; whether this includes every remote original rather than hosting records is not specified and must be verified before relying on it.

features.name: CDN caching and purge integration
features.detail: Cloudflare delivery caches public responses and avoids Range fragments; configured Cloudflare API credentials can purge cached content after deletion/access changes.

features.name: Time-limited hosted-file lifecycle
features.detail: Live docs describe future-upload expiry presets up to 3650 days, optional uploader choice and scheduled/manual cleanup. Application access stops on expiry, while underlying public links/caches can persist; release parity is unverified.

features.name: Disable remote telemetry
features.detail: Admin settings can disable telemetry that may disclose access URLs/domains. v2.7.8 removes remote sampling configuration, not telemetry itself; sampling defaults to 100%.

limitations.text: External provider limits/costs vary; self-hosting this service is not equivalent to offline originals, E2EE or zero third-party processing.
Ordinary file links are generally unauthenticated. Moderation/blacklisting/deletion can lag in CDN caches; direct storage links may bypass hosting access restrictions.

Live expiry docs state Telegram/external-channel cleanup removes only the hosting record, not the remote file. WebDAV-service uploads receive no expiry; public provider URLs remain live until cleanup and cached copies may persist.

Image sizing differs by deployment: JPEG/PNG/WebP everywhere, AVIF Worker/Docker only, GIF resizing Docker only; SVG unsupported. Worker/Docker processing limits originals to 20 MB, and Pages needs enabled Cloudflare transformations plus a custom domain.

AI supports JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF/GIF but not SVG/non-images; manual GIF recognition uses the first decoded frame. Maximum manual batch is 3 with 2 concurrent calls and a 25-second processing deadline; provider format support still applies.
Backup payload completeness, EXIF/IPTC edits, duplicates, face identities and photo semantic search are not established. AI tag recognition is not face recognition or vector search.
Live docs may exceed frozen release functionality; automatic upload AI/expiry marked medium confidence. MOVE appears in overview but not WebDAV method table.

gaps: Live-doc versus v2.7.8 parity unresolved for automatic tagging and expiry.
Dedicated AI URL returned 404; complete AI configuration section and release notes inspected instead.
No live provider or integration tests; backup scope and WebDAV MOVE discrepancy remain.

R11.summary: Read-only self-hosted gallery over existing photo/video folders, with nested folder albums, per-user roots, face grouping and controlled public sharing.
deployment: Docker Compose
Linux server packages/source; documented Debian/Ubuntu, Arch, NixOS and appliance/community integrations
Browser client
R11.storage_model: Originals remain in filesystem directories, which map to albums. Separate database (SQLite, MariaDB or PostgreSQL) holds catalogue/user/share data and a configurable cache holds thumbnails, high-resolution web previews and transcoded video. Example media mounts are read-only.
R11.privacy_model: Originals can remain on the operator's server; users are scoped to assigned roots and media requests use cookie tokens. Optional maps depend on Mapbox token/services. README explicitly warns that basic authentication alone is insufficient protection for Internet exposure and recommends external hardening; no E2EE guarantee is made.
maturity_notes: Frozen master f2f41dfc2333b81fda2025ab5a9c8efb6ffbc662 is substantially newer than v2.4.0 (2024-06-23).
v2.4.0 is described as the project-restart release; current README changes container registry and recommends PostgreSQL 18/17, which must not be retroactively assumed for older deployments.
Hardware acceleration values are documented, but maintainers explicitly verified only Intel QSV. Third-party Docker abstraction support is limited.

features.name: Favorite photos and videos

features.name: Video technical metadata
features.detail: Displays dimensions, duration, codec, frame rate, bitrate, color profile and audio information.

features.name: Album/media text query
features.detail: Search API returns albums and media with separate result limits; inspected contract does not establish semantic or arbitrary EXIF search semantics.

features.name: RAW preview support
features.detail: README documents RAW photography support; release v2.4.0 specifically adds CR3.

features.name: HEIC processing
features.detail: v2.4.0 fixes HEIC EXIF extraction and README lists libheif as a server dependency.

features.name: RAW/web-image counterpart pairing
features.detail: Same-stem compatible JPEG/web images can accompany a RAW/non-web image and be skipped as separate catalogue entries. Disabling RAW processing instead leaves compatible images standalone.

features.name: Sidecar-sensitive RAW previews
features.detail: For non-web-compatible photos, discovers filename.ext.xmp, stores its hash and regenerates JPEG preview/thumbnail when sidecar changes or disappears. This establishes sidecar change detection, not a general XMP field reader/writer or searchable sidecar metadata.

features.name: Browser video playback
features.detail: Video media expose videoWeb resources and are optimized for browser delivery; v2.4.0 improves playback startup.

features.name: Automatic web video optimization
features.detail: Server converts supported video into web-ready resources rather than requiring browser-native support for every original container.

features.name: Optional accelerated FFmpeg
features.detail: Configure qsv, vaapi or nvenc and expose required devices/runtime; only QSV is explicitly maintainer-verified.

features.name: Detect face rectangles
features.detail: Scanner detects faces and schema records normalized bounding boxes; custom builds can omit face support.

features.name: Group people automatically
features.detail: README describes grouping photos of the same person; schema stores face groups and counts.

features.name: Recognize unlabeled faces
features.detail: API can compare unlabeled faces with labeled groups and move matches into those groups.

features.name: Name face groups
features.detail: Set or clear a person's group label.

features.name: Merge, move and detach faces
features.detail: Merge source groups into a destination, move selected faces to another group or detach them into a newly created group.

features.name: Mapbox Places globe
features.detail: MAPBOX_TOKEN enables a globe-projection map of geotagged media with map controls and media viewing; no offline map is established.

features.name: Cluster geotagged media
features.detail: Map's GeoJSON source clusters nearby media with a 50-pixel radius and carries thumbnail properties into marker rendering.

features.name: Multiple users with filesystem scope
features.detail: Create users associated with assigned root paths, separating accessible directory trees.

features.name: Admin/user access controls
features.detail: User administration and scans require admin role; owned-media or valid share credentials authorize catalogue access.

features.name: Share albums or individual media
features.detail: Generate revocable public share tokens, optionally labeled for their owner/administrator.

features.name: Password-protected shares
features.detail: Shares can require a password and have password protection changed or cleared.

features.name: Expiring shares
features.detail: Share creation and update APIs accept an optional expiration time.

features.name: Media download variants
features.detail: Media exposes a list of downloadable file versions with role/title, URL, dimensions and file size; exact variants depend on processing.

features.name: Read-only media access
features.detail: README calls the gallery read-only and Compose mounts media using :ro while cache/database remain separate writable volumes.

features.name: Separate preview cache
features.detail: Generated previews are stored in configurable PHOTOVIEW_MEDIA_CACHE; media can include blurhash placeholders.

features.name: Configurable scan concurrency
features.detail: Admin API sets the maximum concurrent scanner jobs; v2.4.0 also allows scanning to continue after individual-media failure.

features.name: GraphQL catalogue and administration API
features.detail: Typed GraphQL queries/mutations cover catalogue, accounts, scans, faces and share tokens; development mode exposes a playground.

limitations.text: README explicitly warns that basic authentication/read-only gallery access alone is insufficient protection for Internet exposure; TLS, VPN/reverse proxy and other controls are operator responsibilities.

Map features require a Mapbox token and remote provider. Container paths for separate media mounts must not overlap. Large-library speed descriptions and database rankings are project claims, not benchmarks performed here.

Pinned current branch and old latest release differ in database/registry configuration. Simply updating the v2.4.0 container without applying documented configuration changes is explicitly warned against.
No inspected evidence establishes guest uploading, managed import/mobile backup, exact/perceptual duplicate cleanup, semantic/OCR search, embedded-metadata writes or an operation journal.
Lazy image loading is not claimed as row virtualization; counterpart pairing is filename/type association, not content-based duplicate detection.

gaps: No broad semantic/metadata-query semantics inferred from the generic search contract.
User manual coverage is principally comprehensive README and annotated deployment configuration, supplemented by capability schemas and implementations.
No runtime tests of codecs, GPU backends or remote Mapbox.

R12.summary: Original legacy Lychee single-owner photo upload, album management and sharing server; not the modern LycheeOrg application.
deployment: PHP 5.5+ web server and MySQL according to legacy documentation
README recommends a separate community Docker image
R12.storage_model: Managed upload/import directories, thumbnails and optional medium-size derivatives with MySQL albums/photos/settings. FAQ explicitly disallows using an existing folder structure in place. Duplicate uploads can share one physical file or be skipped.
R12.privacy_model: Self-hosted photo storage with owner login and public/private/password album controls. Optional Dropbox imports and social-card sharing use external services. Original-file access hardening is listed as a separate plugin; no E2EE guarantee is established.
maturity_notes: README says development moved to LycheeOrg on 2018-04-01; do not transfer modern fork features here.

Manifest latest release is v3.1.6 from 2017-03-20; pinned master is 9cec5df56be3c06637406d9d83bdffc452f94569, last push 2022. Historical PHP/browser requirements are not current compatibility assurances.

features.name: Browser photo-management interface
features.detail: Legacy Lychee exposes upload, photo/album management and sharing through a browser connected to its PHP/MySQL server. The FAQ lists supported browser families; its historical compatibility list is not a current-version guarantee.

features.name: SSH photo-upload companion
features.detail: README lists the separate lycheeupload extension for uploading photos to Lychee via SSH. This is an advertised companion capability, not a built-in upload transport or independently tested extension.

features.name: Jekyll album embedding extension
features.detail: README lists a separate Jekyll Liquid tag for embedding Lychee albums in generated sites; no current Jekyll-version compatibility was established.

features.name: Human-readable album-name redirect plugin
features.detail: README lists lychee-redirect as a separate extension that redirects an album name to a Lychee album, rather than a core routing guarantee.

features.name: Toshiba FlashAir import extension
features.detail: README lists lychee-FlashAir for importing photos from a Toshiba FlashAir WiFi SD card. Hardware/network setup and current extension compatibility were not separately verified.

features.name: Webroot access-control extension
features.detail: README describes lychee-webroot as a separate extension controlling photo accessibility and keeping Lychee files hidden. Its existence must not be interpreted as default core original-file protection.

features.name: Regenerate missing medium derivatives
features.detail: README lists lychee-create-medium for generating missing medium-size photos; this is an external maintenance extension, not built-in image editing.

features.name: Single-owner web photo manager
features.detail: Runs on the owner's PHP/MySQL server and offers browser upload, management and sharing.

features.name: Community Docker deployment
features.detail: README recommends kdelfour's separate lychee-docker image, not a native desktop/mobile application.

features.name: Upload into a managed library
features.detail: Browser upload supports JPEG, PNG and GIF photos; server uses its own folder structure and database.

features.name: Recursive server-directory import
features.detail: Import accepts a chosen server directory, recurses into subdirectories and creates albums named from folders with an Import prefix; reserved Lychee derivative directories are excluded.

features.name: Import image URLs
features.detail: URL import accepts multiple comma-separated URLs, verifies extension and image type before download, then feeds the managed photo-add path.

features.name: Dropbox import
features.detail: Requires a Dropbox drop-ins application key, requested on first use and configurable later.

features.name: Skip already uploaded photos
features.detail: skipDuplicates setting suppresses uploads of existing photos; older changelog also documents duplicate records sharing one stored file.

features.name: Checksum-based duplicate storage
features.detail: Changelog records stored photo checksums, switch from MD5 to SHA-1, and detection that stores only one file; no perceptual comparison or cleanup review workflow is established.

features.name: Create and manage albums
features.detail: Create albums, rename and describe them, move photos between albums and merge albums; documented hooks and changelog establish each action.

features.name: Built-in smart collections
features.detail: Changelog documents Recent and Unsorted smart albums and downloadable SmartAlbums; arbitrary user-defined query albums are not established.

features.name: Star-driven album covers
features.detail: FAQ says covers are selected automatically from starred photos and upload order; starring an image influences the album thumbnail.

features.name: Editable photo tags
features.detail: Photo tagging is available through the UI and t shortcut; setTags hook exists and IPTC tags can seed imported tags.

features.name: Titles and descriptions
features.detail: Photos and albums expose title/description editing and information panels; these are catalogue fields, not demonstrated embedded writes.

features.name: Star photos
features.detail: Photo shortcut s/f and setStar hook mark favorites, also influencing album covers.

features.name: EXIF information and orientation
features.detail: Imports/displays EXIF including capture date and handles EXIF rotate/flip orientation with GD or Imagick.

features.name: Import IPTC descriptive data
features.detail: Changelog documents headline/caption, title fallback when headline is absent, and photo-tag import.

features.name: Strip metadata from derivatives
features.detail: Imagick path removes metadata from medium images and thumbnails; this does not establish stripping metadata from downloadable originals.

features.name: Search albums and photos
features.detail: Search is available from the album overview; changelog explicitly describes albums shown before photo results. Exact searchable field semantics were not traced.

features.name: Capture-date sorting
features.detail: Changelog documents takedate sorting fixes; settings permit photo ORDER BY field/direction configuration.

features.name: Configurable album/photo sorting
features.detail: sortingAlbums and sortingPhotos store SQL ordering fragments; some settings require direct database editing rather than a UI option.

features.name: Keyboard navigation and multiselect
features.detail: Shortcuts cover previous/next photo, search, metadata editing, favorites, select all, upload and delete.

features.name: Mobile swipe navigation
features.detail: Changelog documents swipe gestures and later touch/swipe fixes.

features.name: Distraction-reduced image view
features.detail: Changelog describes fullscreen entry/exit based on mouse activity and hiding the pointer in fullscreen.

features.name: Public images and albums
features.detail: Share individual photos and albums; hidden shared albums can be reachable only by direct link rather than public listing.

features.name: Password-protected albums
features.detail: Album password setting/checking hooks and password-prompt/download behavior are documented; this is album-level, not a claimed per-image password capability.

features.name: Album download visibility control
features.detail: Public albums can be configured downloadable or not; no claim is made that this prevents saving images already displayed.

features.name: Social preview metadata
features.detail: Shared images, but explicitly not albums, support Twitter Cards and Open Graph; historical Twitter domain approval instructions are not current service guarantees.

features.name: Photo and album downloads
features.detail: Download individual photos and album archives, including smart albums after the v3.1.6 fix; changelog notes title-based download filenames.

features.name: Generated thumbnails and medium images
features.detail: Creates thumbnails; when Imagick is present it additionally provides medium-size images for small screens and documented quality/performance improvements.

features.name: Prefetch adjacent viewing assets
features.detail: Changelog documents preloading large photos then preferring medium images for prefetch, plus album caching and saved scroll positions.

features.name: Documented manual backup
features.detail: FAQ instructs copying the whole installation folder and cloning albums/photos/settings tables; this is a manual procedure, not scheduled backups or a versioned action journal.

features.name: Built-in diagnostics page
features.detail: FAQ points to plugins/Diagnostics/index.php for detected errors; changelog documents configuration/system checks.

features.name: Backend lifecycle hooks
features.detail: Separately registered PHP observers receive before/after album, photo, session and import hooks; docs explicitly say plugins cannot modify the frontend.

features.name: Upload watermark extension
features.detail: README lists lychee-watermark, a separate plugin that adds a second watermarked photo on upload; not normal built-in editing.

features.name: External folder synchronization
features.detail: README lists lycheesync as a separate extension for syncing an existing photo directory; this does not remove core managed-storage limitations.

features.name: Photo RSS feed extension
features.detail: README lists lychee-rss as a separate feed-generating extension.

features.name: Core in-place source browsing
features.detail: FAQ explicitly says the app cannot use the existing folder structure and requires upload/import into its own storage/database.

features.name: Video library support
features.detail: FAQ says videos cannot be uploaded and video support is not planned for this legacy application.

features.name: Multiple owner accounts
features.detail: FAQ explicitly answers no/not yet to creating multiple users; public album viewers are not independent owner accounts.

limitations.text: This repository is legacy; contemporary LycheeOrg features must not be attributed to it.
Existing folders, video uploads and multiple users are explicitly unsupported in the FAQ; only PNG, JPEG and GIF uploads are listed.
Core metadata embedded-write behavior is not established: plugin docs give writing changes back as a customization use case, not an installed capability.
Photos use PHP upload/time/memory limits; large uploads may need server configuration changes. Some settings are database-only.
No inspected evidence establishes face recognition, maps, perceptual matching, app trash/undo, E2EE, or expiry-based shares.

gaps: Modern LycheeOrg intentionally excluded.
Listed third-party plugins were not individually audited; only their advertised role is recorded.
Search field details and current runtime compatibility not established.

R13.summary: Local Takeout repair/organization utility that deduplicates exports, reconstructs albums and restores filesystem dates; current Dart version does not write JSON metadata into EXIF.
deployment: Windows executable
macOS executable (README instructs Rosetta on Apple Silicon)
Linux executable/AUR package
Interactive prompts or headless CLI
R13.storage_model: Consumes manually extracted, merged Takeout trees; moves by default or copies into ALL_PHOTOS and album directories, optionally year/month subfolders. Albums use shortcuts/symlinks, duplicate files or an albums-info.json manifest. There is no persistent browsable catalogue.
R13.privacy_model: Processing works on local export files; obtaining Takeout is a prior Google service step. No mandatory third-party media upload appears in the documented workflow. Recommended ExifTool/Syncthing/other galleries are separate tools, not built-in features.
maturity_notes: Frozen commit a9de187efd9ce7cd072c5803dabc45079d416e64; latest release v3.4.3 (2023-09-24), code version also 3.4.3.
Dart rewrite supersedes legacy Python v2.x; older Python GPS/EXIF writing must not be attributed to current Dart.
Source inspection exposes a significant >64 MiB hashing limitation; no execution or empirical safety test was performed.
