features.name: Translated desktop interface
features.detail: GUI dynamically discovers bundled locale JSON files and reloads strings when CurrentLanguage changes; French menus, dialogs and result columns are explicitly translated. Default/load-failure fallback is English, while missing individual keys display the key. Localization parity for CLI/web is not inferred.

features.name: Visual video duplicate matching
features.detail: Finds related video content despite different resolution/frame rate and watermarks using sampled visual similarity rather than byte equality.

features.name: Image similarity matching
features.detail: Image scanning is supported alongside videos; CLI --include-images is off by default, while the core settings default includes images.

features.name: Classic algorithm and threshold controls
features.detail: Choose grayscale percentage-difference or pHash, or combine both so either match qualifies. Controls include hash-difference threshold, minimum similarity and required fraction of matching sampled pHash frames.

features.name: Flip/background matching controls
features.detail: Core settings expose horizontal-flip comparison and ignoring black/white pixels, distinct from optional neural transformed-copy detection.

features.name: Audio-based partial video detection
features.detail: A second phase uses chroma fingerprints and sliding-window Hamming similarity to find shorter clips within longer sources, reports a Clip Offset and defaults to visual confirmation at the offset. Both files need audio.

features.name: Clip duration/audio/visual thresholds
features.detail: Audio clip mode defaults to minimum 10% clip/source duration, 80% audio similarity and 85% frame confirmation; the confirmation requirement is independently configurable.

features.name: Neural transformed-copy detection
features.detail: DINOv2 embeddings via ONNX add matches for cropped, mirrored, zoomed, letterboxed or heavily edited copies; classic results remain authoritative and are never hidden by enabling AI. Default threshold is 94%.

features.name: Silent/retimed clip matching
features.detail: Independent AI partial-detection switch compares dense keyframes by a consistent time offset; at least four hits must agree, default frame threshold 89%. Works without audio, including muted/re-dubbed clips.

features.name: CPU-local optional AI
features.detail: ONNX runtime/model download is about 100 MB once; model is checked against pinned SHA256. GUI asks before download; enabled CLI/web/Docker auto-download. No content is sent to a cloud AI account.

features.name: Reusable scan database
features.detail: Stores fingerprints for fast rescanning; optional embeddings are cached at roughly 2 KB/file, with dense keyframes in a separately cleaned sidecar at a claimed 25 KB/video.

features.name: Remember deleted content
features.detail: Optional RememberDeletedContent retains fingerprints when the last copy is deleted, so re-downloaded content can be recognized; database cleanup becomes tombstone-aware. This is not a general reviewed-pair ignore list.

features.name: Compare against prior/missing files
features.detail: Settings can scan against the entire database and include non-existing files; tombstone mode also enables missing-file comparison.

features.name: Multiple input directories
features.detail: CLI accepts repeatable include directories and core settings control recursive scanning.

features.name: Path and filesystem exclusions
features.detail: Exclude directories, apply contains/not-contains path filters and optionally ignore read-only folders, reparse points or existing hard links.

features.name: File-size restrictions
features.detail: Core scan settings expose enabled minimum/maximum file-size filtering.

features.name: Same/different-folder matching
features.detail: FolderMatchMode permits unrestricted, same-folder-only or different-folder-only matching with configurable same-folder depth.

features.name: Duration candidate constraints
features.detail: Configure percentage duration tolerance with minimum/maximum seconds bounds; with percentage disabled, seconds-only tolerance is supported. Maximum sampled duration is also configurable.

features.name: Automatic quality/size keeper rules
features.detail: CLI can retain highest bitrate/resolution, largest file, longest duration or highest resolution per group. A 100-percent-only strategy acts only on fully matching reported groups; that label is not independently proven byte equality.

features.name: Default action preview
features.detail: CLI action workflow defaults to dry-run and explicitly recommends reviewing before automatic deletion.

features.name: Trash instead of permanent removal
features.detail: CLI --delete moves selected duplicates to trash; permanent deletion requires the distinct --delete-permanent option. Platform/container trash availability is not fully detailed.

features.name: Text/JSON/CSV reports
features.detail: CLI writes selected text, JSON or CSV output to stdout or a named file and can load comprehensive JSON settings.

features.name: Group-aware path filtering
features.detail: GUI path search is case-insensitive substring matching or unanchored * and ? wildcards; matching a member preserves the surrounding duplicate group.

features.name: Result type filter
features.detail: GUI filters results to all, videos or images.

features.name: Similarity and selected-group filters
features.detail: Result filters support minimum/maximum similarity and groups with checked items.

features.name: Review AI-added groups
features.detail: An AI filter retains groups containing an AI-only accepted member along with its comparison context; it is not an AI-only rescan.

features.name: Hide resolved groups safely
features.detail: Can hide groups with at most one remaining existing member; files on disconnected drives still count as offline rather than deleted.

features.name: Generated preview thumbnails
features.detail: Core settings expose generation of preview thumbnails with count and maximum width, supporting visual inspection of similarity results.

features.name: Storage-aware hashing concurrency
features.detail: Separate read/hashing and CPU matching limits; slow/network drives default to a low per-drive cap while SSDs share the global budget. Automatic drive classification can be overridden.

features.name: Periodic scan database saves
features.detail: Automatic checkpoint interval defaults to five minutes; zero disables interval saves but retains phase-boundary saves. This is not a file-operation undo journal.

features.name: Optional native FFmpeg bindings
features.detail: Can call FFmpeg functions natively for claimed speed improvement; requires compatible FFmpeg 8.x shared libraries rather than master builds.

features.name: Headless automation
features.detail: Separate scan/compare and combined CLI workflows are suitable for scripts and scheduled jobs without a display.

features.name: Local/LAN web interface
features.detail: Self-contained web server supports headless/NAS access, configurable listening port, generated or configured password and optional 30-day remember-me cookie.

features.name: Multi-architecture Docker deployment
features.detail: Web image bundles FFmpeg, supports amd64/arm64 and separates persistent settings/database from mounted media; numbered tags avoid rolling latest.

features.name: Read-only container media mounts
features.detail: Documented Docker examples and guidance recommend :ro media mounts for scan-only safety; deletion needs a writable configuration.

features.name: No mandatory content upload
features.detail: All documented comparison occurs on the scanning machine, with optional model/runtime downloads but no cloud content-analysis service.

limitations.text: Web UI is password-protected but explicitly not intended for public Internet exposure; authentication can be disabled by an environment variable.
Audio clip detection skips videos without audio; optional visual AI is a separate solution and can produce false positives at looser thresholds.
FFmpeg/FFprobe are required; optional native binding and AI have additional runtime/download requirements.
Automatic deletion is discouraged by the project. Perceptual/AI or reported 100% matching is not established as cryptographic whole-file identity.
Metadata editing, photo albums, face recognition, maps, playback integration, duplicate-link replacement and a general operation journal are not established by the inspected sources.

gaps: Primary detailed user manual is embedded in README; source clarifies additional current-branch options.
Features from the pinned branch are not all asserted to ship in stable v4.1.1; no execution/performance tests performed.

R25.summary: Nextcloud-integrated photo/video timeline with metadata editing, maps, albums, advanced media formats and optional recognition/transcoding services.
deployment: Nextcloud app with responsive browser UI
NativeX Android client on Google Play/F-Droid/GitHub
Optional go-vod Docker service
Optional current-source Lens semantic-search daemon and Qdrant
R25.storage_model: Originals remain in Nextcloud's existing folder structure, including configured external/object storage. Memories stores metadata indexes in the Nextcloud database, uses preview derivatives and optionally caches video keyframes/storyboards. Archive moves files into .archive rather than merely toggling a database flag.
R25.privacy_model: Data remains on the device and chosen Nextcloud/services, not necessarily on a single local machine. Recognition depends on separately configured apps; optional Lens executes its embedding model on the chosen daemon. Reverse geocoding uses an imported local planet dataset, while map tiles/location search can contact configured providers. Nextcloud server-side encryption support is not E2EE. The website-oriented privacy policy also describes web logs and third-party libraries, so no blanket no-telemetry claim is made.
maturity_notes: Frozen master commit a17051a1e63cf6aa1a8dce1d3eec061d8b89cb25; latest release v11.1.1 published 2026-11-09 (changelog dates it 2026-11-08).
Current series requires Nextcloud 34+ per v9 release history. App, Android and go-vod have separate tags/version compatibility.
Lens exists with setup/source in this snapshot but is not announced in the inspected release history; its packaged release availability is unverified.
Current VIPS support supersedes older ImageMagick/RAW-plugin setup instructions. Comparison page explicitly labels itself outdated; no competitor claims are used.
Million-photo testing and recent speedup ratios are developer claims, not benchmarks performed here.

features.name: Multilingual Nextcloud interface
features.detail: Release history explicitly adds localization with many languages from v2.0 and later localized metadata dates; README links the application's Transifex translation workflow. Separate from optional multilingual Lens queries.

features.name: Nextcloud app
features.detail: Install through Nextcloud's app store, configure the admin panel and index existing files; not a standalone service independent of Nextcloud.

features.name: Responsive browser application
features.detail: Browser UI works on desktop and Android/iOS with touch layouts; a native iOS Memories binary is not claimed.

features.name: Android NativeX client
features.detail: Available through Google Play, F-Droid and separate GitHub Android releases; latest notes add mTLS client certificates and optional HDR disable.

features.name: Optional Docker companion services
features.detail: Hardware-transcoding guide provides a separate radialapps/go-vod Docker service alongside Nextcloud; current-source Lens setup provides Docker Compose for its daemon and Qdrant. These are optional companions, not evidence that Memories is a standalone photo-server image independent of Nextcloud.

features.name: Preserve existing Nextcloud files
features.detail: Uses existing files and their metadata without requiring a second proprietary original store; folder hierarchy remains intact.

features.name: Multiple timeline roots and mounted storage
features.detail: Configure multiple timeline paths and recursively include mounted volumes/shares within them; this is one user's scope, not separate catalogues.

features.name: Folder-preserving timeline
features.detail: Flat date display is layered on the unchanged directory hierarchy, with optional folder browsing.

features.name: Incremental indexing and upload hooks
features.detail: Background jobs and immediate upload hooks index new/changed files. External modifications may need Nextcloud files:scan first; rerunning memories:index is incremental unless forced.

features.name: Web and Android manual uploads
features.detail: Direct web upload, Android destination-folder upload and selected local photo uploads are documented in release history.

features.name: Automatic upload through Nextcloud clients
features.detail: README directs automatic camera/photo/video upload to official Nextcloud Android/iOS apps rather than attributing background backup to Memories itself.

features.name: Google Takeout metadata migration
features.detail: OCC command copies Takeout JSON into EXIF, optionally overriding existing fields and scoped by user/folder; it modifies source files and documentation requires backups.

features.name: Move or copy selected media
features.detail: Move from timeline to folders and, since 7.5.1, copy rather than move; copying triggers immediate indexing in later releases.

features.name: Organize into year-month folders
features.detail: Move-to-folder workflow can organize selected files by year and month.

features.name: Archive outside ordinary timeline
features.detail: Archive moves photos to .archive at timeline/storage root, which may be mounted to cold storage; this is a filesystem move, not just hiding.

features.name: Index and visibility exclusions
features.detail: Supports .nomedia, app-specific .nomemories, hidden folders/files, regex filename/folder patterns and MIME blocklist; v11.1.1 fixes name-blocklist application to files.

features.name: Download media, albums and folders
features.detail: Individual and whole album/public album/folder downloads are documented; v10 adds resumable file downloads.

features.name: EXIF date timeline and direct date jumps
features.detail: Sort photos/videos by capture date with a scrubber and #day/yyyy-mm-dd links; memories can jump to the corresponding day.

features.name: Capture-date ordering
features.detail: Uses EXIF date rather than filesystem modification time; GPS can supply timezone information when camera EXIF lacks it.

features.name: Virtual scrolling timeline
features.detail: Official feature explanation explicitly identifies infinite virtual scrolling plus random-access date scrubber; no benchmark is inferred.

features.name: Breadcrumb and recursive folder views
features.detail: Choose folder-view root, use breadcrumbs, optionally show a recursive timeline, and browse folders within shares.

features.name: On-this-day resurfacing
features.detail: Past photos appear in an On this day view and optionally at the top of the timeline, with age and direct-day navigation.

features.name: Bulk selection and mobile gestures
features.detail: Select entire days, shift-click or touch-drag, pinch/scroll zoom and swipe-to-refresh; later releases preserve navigation scroll position.

features.name: Desktop fullscreen viewer
features.detail: Fullscreen viewing includes Shift+F keyboard shortcut and photo deep links.

features.name: High-resolution image and video zoom
features.detail: Full image can load upon zoom with configurable administrator defaults; desktop mouse wheel and newer video zoom are supported.

features.name: Photo/video slideshow
features.detail: Slideshow supports photos and videos with optional metadata display.

features.name: PhotoSphere viewer
features.detail: v10 introduces interactive PhotoSphere panorama viewing; not a generic inference from a 2:1 image.

features.name: Adaptive or direct video playback
features.detail: Browser-supported codecs play directly; optional HLS transcoding handles other formats, with quality selection/fallback and user/admin autoplay controls.

features.name: Video timeline hover previews
features.detail: go-vod generates thumbnail sprites/VTT storyboards for video hover previews, cached persistently with keyframes.

features.name: Bundled camera RAW previews
features.detail: Current VIPS provider supports RAW out of the box and can be disabled. Older camera-raw-preview app is a fallback, not a current mandatory dependency.

features.name: HEIC and HEIF previews
features.detail: Bundled VIPS handles HEIC/HEIF with no extra image dependency when enabled; older provider fallback requires ImageMagick support.

features.name: AVIF support
features.detail: VIPS decodes AVIF; old files may require MIME repair and reindexing after upgrade. Editor also offers AVIF output.

features.name: Ultra-HDR, Samsung HDR and colour profiles
features.detail: v11 VIPS decoder supports Ultra-HDR/Samsung HDR and ICC profiles; Android offers HDR-display disable.

features.name: Apple Live Photos
features.detail: Paired live-photo viewing, autoplay/loop settings and editing via a separate copy; earlier JPEG-only limitations are superseded by later HEVC/HEIC handling.

features.name: Google, Samsung and Huawei motion formats
features.detail: Release history documents Google MVIMG, Samsung HEIC Motion Photos and Huawei Moving Picture.

features.name: RAW companion stacking
features.detail: Can hide/stack RAWs beside another same-basename file; current releases support metadata edits of stacked JPEG+RAW pairs.

features.name: EXIF sidebar and timeline metadata
features.detail: Bundled ExifTool extracts photo/video capture and technical metadata, displayed in sidebar and used for timeline/maps.

features.name: Edit original metadata
features.detail: Supports changing EXIF dates, title/description and GPS; RAW metadata editing is added in v11. These are source-file edits, not a default read-only catalogue.

features.name: Bulk metadata and rotation
features.detail: Bulk date/other EXIF edits and collaborative tags; lossless bulk rotation writes orientation metadata rather than re-encoding pixels.

features.name: Correct capture dates
features.detail: Edit EXIF date individually/in bulk, with a warning when a metadata edit would lose the date.

features.name: Edit photo location
features.detail: GPS editing supports precise coordinates and a configurable location-search provider.

features.name: Nextcloud collaborative tags
features.detail: Edit/create collaborative tags individually or in bulk and show tags in sidebar; existing Nextcloud tags carry over.

features.name: Favourite media
features.detail: Select and favourite/unfavourite files, with a dedicated Favorites view.

features.name: Nextcloud photo albums
features.detail: Create albums of photos/videos, add to multiple albums, choose covers and sort lists; configuration explicitly requires the Nextcloud Photos app for album support.

features.name: People views from recognition apps
features.detail: People grouping comes from Recognize or alternative Face Recognition app, with face thumbnails in sidebar and selectable person covers.

features.name: Recognize/Face Recognition integration
features.detail: Uses separately installed Nextcloud Recognize or Face Recognition; alternative Face Recognition integration is described as alpha with extra fine-tuning.

features.name: Rename identified people
features.detail: Release history documents naming/renaming Recognize face groups rather than merely face detection.

features.name: Merge and move faces
features.detail: Merge face clusters, move photos between people, move unclustered faces and create a new cluster while moving; version requirements belong to Recognize.

features.name: Recognize object tags
features.detail: Object/tag grouping is provided by Recognize rather than a built-in mandatory AI engine.

features.name: Basic built-in search
features.detail: v7.1 introduces basic search and album-picker/face-merge dialogs have search. Exact full-library query grammar is not established by these docs.

features.name: Optional Lens natural-language search
features.detail: Current-source Lens guide describes multilingual image description search after indexing, requiring a dedicated non-admin service account, separate daemon and Qdrant. Packaged release parity remains unverified.

features.name: Lens model inference on chosen daemon
features.detail: Lens caches a pinned model snapshot and runs normalized image/text embeddings locally in its daemon, on CPU or CUDA. Initial model provisioning accesses Hugging Face unless complete offline cache exists.

features.name: CUDA Lens embedding option
features.detail: Lens embedding backend selects CUDA when configured/available, with Float16 there and Float32 CPU fallback.

features.name: Collapse presumed duplicate timeline entries
features.detail: De-duplicate identical files setting collapses matching AUID entries and retains hidden copies for bulk actions. Missing AUID is derived from MD5(timestamp plus file size), not file bytes; this is presentation deduplication, not verified exact-content cleanup.

features.name: Photo map with selectable tile source
features.detail: GPS-tagged photo map, configurable tile server, high-precision marker setting and Android local-photo geolocation; no bundled offline basemap established.

features.name: Local planet-boundary reverse geocoding
features.detail: Download/import planet database into MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL for server-side place lookup; can supply a custom planet ZIP. Map tiles remain an independent feature.

features.name: Hierarchical places and missing-location view
features.detail: Places hierarchy and a filter for files without location, with configurable place covers; named places depend on geocoder setup.

features.name: Nextcloud users and authentication
features.detail: Uses Nextcloud user/auth ecosystem rather than reimplementing accounts; README and FAQ explicitly support multiple users.

features.name: External photo, album and folder shares
features.detail: Share individual or selected media and folders externally; album shares use Photos dependency and can be shared with Nextcloud users/groups or public links.

features.name: Password-protected shares
features.detail: Password-protected folder shares and fixes for password link shares are explicitly documented.

features.name: Upload to public shares
features.detail: v7.8 adds upload to public shares; v9 fixes video uploads there. Availability still follows the underlying share permissions.

features.name: High/low-resolution and native sharing
features.detail: Share at high/low resolution, use native share interface, and transcode shared videos to smaller outputs.

features.name: Server-side crop and straighten
features.detail: Current VIPS editor offers free/original/fixed aspect ratios and straightening from −45° to +45° in half-degree steps.

features.name: Rotate and flip images
features.detail: Editor state supports rotation and horizontal/vertical flips; separate bulk rotation updates EXIF losslessly.

features.name: Tone, colour, detail and presets
features.detail: Brightness, exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, saturation, vibrance, hue, temperature, blur, sharpen and vignette, plus warm/cool/monochrome/negative presets.

features.name: JPEG, PNG and AVIF editor output
features.detail: Save dialog offers JPEG/PNG/AVIF, with 90/85/75 quality presets for lossy output and lossless PNG.

features.name: Save edited copies
features.detail: Choose copy versus explicit overwrite; Live Photos always create copies and format changes force copy mode. This is save-as safety, not a full reversible edit recipe.

features.name: Optional live HLS transcoding
features.detail: go-vod adapts resolution to connection speed, supports quality selection and direct HLS-fMP4 streaming of HEVC/AV1/VP9. Disabled by default; CPU fallback without hardware.

features.name: VA-API and NVENC acceleration
features.detail: Intel QuickSync/compatible VA-API and NVIDIA NVENC require device/drivers/FFmpeg; newer NVENC uses Jellyfin GPU HDR tone mapping.

features.name: External and distributed transcoding
features.detail: Deploy separate go-vod containers/hosts and list several addresses for load distribution with per-client sticky routing; supports external/object storage with documented setup.

features.name: Preview pipelining and cache
features.detail: Preview derivatives and optimized loading reduce repeated work; optional Preview Generator app pre-generates previews. Sizes/quality are configurable and may otherwise exceed compact originals.

features.name: Parallel metadata indexing
features.detail: Run multiple memories:index processes concurrently; can scope to user/group/path to avoid full-library work.

features.name: Retry and refresh selected metadata
features.detail: CLI supports retry failed entries, forced refresh or clear/reindex; UI supports Refresh Metadata on selected photos and lists failures in admin settings.

features.name: Trash restore and permanent delete
features.detail: v10.2 adds a Trash view for restoring or permanently deleting photos within the Nextcloud-backed application; retention is not specified here.

features.name: Configurable deletion confirmation
features.detail: Viewer deletion confirmation exists; v11 allows opting out. Metadata editor warns when a date would be lost.

features.name: Nextcloud server-side encryption compatibility
features.detail: Release history documents support for server-side encrypted storage. Encryption is supplied/configured by Nextcloud, and server-side readable originals are not E2EE.

features.name: Basic cached offline browsing
features.detail: Release history documents basic offline support through cache, not a complete offline original-library replica.

features.name: Administrative OCC commands
features.detail: Index, reverse-geocoder setup and Takeout migration are documented command-line actions; deprecated OCCWeb is explicitly incompatible.

limitations.text: Requires Nextcloud; albums require Photos, AI people/objects require Recognize or Face Recognition, and automatic mobile backup uses Nextcloud mobile clients.
Reverse geocoding does not support SQLite and needs a downloaded planet dataset. It is separate from network-served map tiles; offline basemap support is not established.

External-storage indexing downloads every file and may be slow. Transcoding is disabled by default, compute/storage intensive and documented as unsuitable for Raspberry Pi; failures can fall back to original streams.
Takeout migration and metadata edits modify files; backups are required before migration. Ordinary editor saves can overwrite originals unless copy mode is chosen/forced.

The UI's identical-file dedupe is not proof of content identity: source derives fallback AUID from date and size and collapses display entries, retaining copies for bulk actions. No exact-hash deletion feature is claimed.
Lens optional source functionality and its packaging maturity are not established by release notes; model downloads and chosen daemon/Qdrant are additional dependencies.

No durable per-file-operation recovery journal, E2EE guarantee, GPX synchronization or sidecar-write workflow is established. FAQ de-prioritizes advanced professional XMP/metadata features rather than promising them.

gaps: Lens packaged release availability and exact basic-search fields unresolved.
No live Nextcloud/provider/hardware test; developer performance claims remain attributed.

R26.summary: Database-free PHP image host for personal or guest uploading, transformations, moderation and server-side file administration rather than a complex multi-user photo library.
deployment: Self-hosted PHP web application; Linux/Nginx recommended
PHP 7.4 minimum; documented supported range 7.4–8.4
Community Docker distribution linked by project
R26.storage_model: Files normally reside under a configurable image root with year/month/day paths. PHP configuration files, filesystem counts, logs and caches replace a required database. Optional uploader/admin/token directory separation and FTP configuration exist; application recycle and suspect-image areas retain moved files.
R26.privacy_model: Can host original content on one's server, but optional ModerateContent, TinyPNG, FTP, CDN and nsfwjs services change data flow. Default config includes an external Baidu analytics footer. Upload IP logging/geolocation and publicly exposed statistics are configurable. Source-link protection is not media-at-rest encryption.
maturity_notes: Frozen master 5f3e08bb0af55b70deddf2ef86fa3535aa5dd627; manifest latest release 2.8.7 dated 2026-10-27.

Release 2.8.7 reports major security/stability fixes and deliberately breaks old password hashes, sessions and encrypted deletion/source-protection links; release notes also describe a reissued tag on October 28.
README explicitly targets personal/guest hosting and says it is unsuitable for complex multi-user scenarios.

features.name: Simplified/Traditional Chinese interface conversion
features.detail: Setting language=1 loads the bundled jquery.s2t script and converts page elements to Traditional Chinese. This is a built-in Chinese-script conversion option; English or a broader translated UI catalogue is not established by this evidence.

features.name: Database-free self-hosting
features.detail: PHP application does not require a database; README recommends Linux with Nginx and lists required PHP extensions.

features.name: Responsive browser uploader
features.detail: HTML5 desktop/mobile upload UI returns reusable links; README retains legacy-browser fallback language.

features.name: Community Docker deployment
features.detail: Project documentation links DDS-Derek/EasyImage-Docker rather than establishing an official core image.

features.name: Multi-file drag-and-drop upload
features.detail: Upload queue supports multiple files and HTML5 drag-and-drop; defaults configure 30 files per upload and 10 MiB per file, adjustable subject to PHP limits.

features.name: Optional chunked uploads
features.detail: chunks configuration enables split uploads; release 2.8.7 fixes large-file chunk merging into the wrong directory.

features.name: Date-based managed storage
features.detail: Default storage root is /i/ with year/month/day folders; configuration warns changing that structure can impair operations.

features.name: Uploader/admin/token separation
features.detail: Separate upload-user, administrator and token-ID directories; the public square excludes those separated uploads and lists guest uploads only.

features.name: Guest or login-only uploads
features.detail: Guest hosting is a primary scenario; mustLogin switches to authenticated-only uploads, with optional daily counts and IP restrictions.

features.name: Administrator and upload-only users
features.detail: Create accounts restricted to uploading while administrative file/configuration operations require admin identity; this is not a full collaborative account system.

features.name: Upload size, count and dimension limits
features.detail: Configure daily uploads, per-upload count/size, allowed extensions and minimum/maximum pixel dimensions.

features.name: IP allow/block controls
features.detail: Upload IP blacklists/whitelists are supported; trusted_proxy configuration added with fixes to prevent spoofed forwarding headers bypassing limits.

features.name: Direct and embed links
features.detail: Return direct URL, Markdown, BBCode and HTML links with copying; API also supplies thumbnail and deletion links.

features.name: Token upload API
features.detail: Enable API uploads and POST multipart image plus token. Response includes original filename, URL, thumbnail, deletion link and token ID; optional token-ID filename suffix is documented in 2.8.7.

features.name: PicGo web-uploader plugin
features.detail: Separate PicGo web-uploader plugin maps image/token fields and the response URL after enabling API upload.

features.name: Optional FTP transfer settings
features.detail: Configuration includes remote FTP host, port, passive/SSL mode, local-after-transfer deletion and synchronized remote deletion; deletion controller invokes the FTP delete hook. End-to-end transfer behavior was not runtime-tested.

features.name: Configured non-image uploads
features.detail: Add extensions such as MP4, PDF or MP3 and disable image-only mode to upload other types. This does not establish a video/audio playback library.

features.name: Configurable image compression
features.detail: Set image quality/compression and image-size reduction; configuration also offers a separate TinyPNG service key.

features.name: Upload dimension transformation
features.detail: Configure target width/height, ratio, crop and quality settings for uploaded image transformations.

features.name: Upload format conversion
features.detail: Convert uploaded images to a specified format, subject to server image-library support.

features.name: Text or image watermark
features.detail: Configure text/image watermark, position, font, size and color.

features.name: Generated thumbnail delivery
features.detail: Thumbnail generation has configurable dimensions and is exposed by the upload API; 2.8.7 fixes thumbnail/backend compression behavior.

features.name: Public square and image details
features.detail: Online gallery/administration and per-image information are documented; optional user/token/admin directory separation changes what appears publicly.

features.name: Dark appearance option
features.detail: Default site configuration exposes dark-mode and theme settings.

features.name: Configurable EXIF information display
features.detail: show_exif_info configuration controls image information display; no embedded-metadata editing workflow is established.

features.name: Remote ModerateContent review
features.detail: Enable configured ModerateContent key and moderation mode to classify uploads. The manual's registration instructions were not validated against current provider availability.

features.name: Separate nsfwjs moderation service
features.detail: Can deploy an nsfwjs REST container or compatible endpoint returning Drawing/Hentai/Neutral/Porn/Sexy probabilities; this is a separate service, not in-process local inference.

features.name: Recycle area and restoration
features.detail: With image_recycl enabled, capability-link deletes move files to recycle storage. Admin supports recycle, restore and permanent deletion, including bulk actions.

features.name: Restore moderation-quarantined images
features.detail: Administrative suspic_reimg action restores files from the suspect-image area independently of the ordinary recycle area.

features.name: Uploader deletion links
features.detail: API returns an authorized deletion link usable without admin login. Version 2.8.7 redesigns capability tokens with authenticated encryption and separate delete/hide purposes; this encrypts tokens, not stored pictures.

features.name: Accurate batch-delete outcomes
features.detail: Bulk deletion reports complete success, partial failure or total failure and returns failed paths instead of always claiming success.

features.name: Protected original-image links
features.detail: Configurable source protection uses keyed links; 2.8.7 changes token/key handling and invalidates old links. FAQ warns web-server image caching can cause 404 behavior.

features.name: Separate media hostname
features.detail: Bind an image domain directly to the image root to hide /i/ in returned paths; it must differ from the site domain for this mode.

features.name: Site and storage statistics
features.detail: Website charts/statistics are documented; optional public API can expose selected daily/monthly file counts, folders and used/free/total storage data.

features.name: Upload logs and IP location
features.detail: Upload logs support uploader IP geolocation; release updates ip2region data and removes password/hash material from login logs.

features.name: Cached filesystem statistics
features.detail: 2.8.7 caches/iterates square file counts, general file counting and version checks to avoid recursive full-directory scans on every request; not a measured benchmark.

features.name: Administrative cache refresh
features.detail: Admin controller supports resetting PHP OPcache when available and deleting cached version information.

features.name: Configurable page and advertising content
features.detail: Site title/description, notices, custom code, header/footer advertisements and footer content are configurable.

limitations.text: Not intended for complex multi-user use; uploader roles and directory separation should not be equated with private album permissions.
2.8.7 disables file-manager online editing, archive download and remote fetching. Older feature descriptions of those functions are not current capabilities.
Upgrades to 2.8.7 invalidate old passwords, sessions and deletion/source-protection links; required configuration and PHP migration steps are explicit.
Operators must deny web access to credentials/configuration and script execution in upload directories. Nginx/Caddy/Lighttpd do not apply Apache .htaccess protections automatically.
External analytics are present in default footer configuration. Optional external compression/moderation/FTP/CDN integrations preclude assuming entirely offline or third-party-free operation.
No inspected evidence establishes duplicate discovery, face recognition, semantic search, album taxonomy, metadata writing, encrypted media storage or a durable operation journal.

gaps: Backend-management document is mainly a screenshot; substantive capabilities were verified against README, detailed manuals, configuration and deletion source.
FTP guide is only a short troubleshooting list; FTP integration evidence is configuration plus deletion hooks, not runtime verification.
External-service availability and current pricing were not independently tested.

R27.summary: Desktop uploader and cloud-file manager with local upload history, image processing, multiple destinations, resumable task/finalization workflows and configuration/gallery synchronization; not a conventional photo-library server.
deployment: Windows x64/ARM64 installer and portable packages
macOS Intel/Apple Silicon DMG/ZIP
Linux AppImage, deb, rpm and snap release artifacts
Separate PicList-Core supplies CLI/Docker server; PicHoro is a companion Android client
R27.storage_model: Electron data directory or portable data folder stores data.json upload settings, manage.json cloud accounts, piclist.db upload-history records, taskQueue.json, finalization recovery data and scripts. Actual objects live at selected local/cloud destinations. Gallery sync moves records, not stored objects; management lists actual remote files.
R27.privacy_model: Can use local storage but normally uploads to explicitly configured services. Credentials can be present in config exports, sync backups and mobile QR codes. Clipboard monitoring can automatically upload screenshots; scripts/plugins have file/network access. Local preview cache is loopback-only, not a public image host.
maturity_notes: Manifest release v3.6.1 (2026-10-14); inspected dev 9f302d05e91aed2c1e34680d3c88147b5b1b8474 and official live manual.
v3.6.1 explicitly removes the old built-in web upload page/general-purpose web server; local HTTP upload API and preview service remain.
Uploader, gallery deletion adapter and cloud management support are separate capability sets. Docker/CLI belong to PicList-Core, not this desktop repository.

features.name: Separate PicHoro Android companion
features.detail: README identifies PicHoro as the separate Android mobile client, and the sync guide documents transferring configuration to it by QR code. This is a companion project, not an Android build of the PicList Electron desktop application.

features.name: Separate PicList-Core command-line interface
features.detail: PicList-Core supplies the separately usable CLI, including an interactive terminal interface, setup wizard and named upload/configuration choices described in the release notes. The Electron desktop repository is not itself a standalone CLI distribution; Core requires its documented Node.js runtime.

features.name: Selectable interface language
features.detail: Official configuration guide lets users choose language in System settings; v3.6.1 fixes stale interface text after switching languages. Complete language coverage is not enumerated in these inspected sources.

features.name: Windows desktop distributions
features.detail: Release offers x64/ARM64 installers and ZIP/7z portable builds; README also lists winget/Scoop.

features.name: macOS desktop
features.detail: Intel and Apple Silicon DMG/ZIP releases; menu-bar/main-window behavior documented.

features.name: Linux desktop
features.detail: AppImage, deb, rpm and snap release artifacts; clipboard behavior varies under Linux/WSL/headless sessions.

features.name: Portable local data directory
features.detail: PORTABLE marker beside executable selects adjacent data directory instead of Electron user-data location.

features.name: File and clipboard upload
features.detail: Drag/drop, multi-file selection, clipboard images, absolute paths and file URLs upload to chosen named configuration; arbitrary files depend on provider size/type restrictions.

features.name: Remote URL rehosting
features.detail: Downloads one direct HTTP(S) image URL per line and uploads to destination; explicitly not webpage screenshot capture.

features.name: Automatic clipboard image uploads
features.detail: Optional monitoring uploads newly copied images automatically, including temporary screenshots; docs warn about online destination exposure.

features.name: Second upload destination
features.detail: Can reuse primary processed bytes or independently process original input using secondary settings. Errors are separate and identical configuration can be skipped; not a backfill of earlier uploads.

features.name: Multiple named provider configurations
features.detail: Maintain multiple accounts/configurations per provider; setting default is separate from saving, and up to six favorites enable quick switching.

features.name: Object/cloud storage clients
features.detail: Upload/deletion/management support includes S3/R2/MinIO, OSS, COS, Qiniu and Upyun; Doge Cloud management uses the S3 client. Requires service credentials.

features.name: WebDAV upload and management
features.detail: WebDAV supports upload, remote gallery deletion and cloud management; credentials and serving URLs remain separate from loopback previews.

features.name: Local filesystem upload destination
features.detail: Built-in local destination supports upload, destination-file deletion and file management. Core release notes describe writing to a temporary file before replacing the local destination to reduce incomplete output after interruption.

features.name: SFTP upload and file management
features.detail: Configured SFTP destination supports upload, remote gallery deletion and cloud file management. Core release notes describe temporary-file writes before replacement and recursive folder downloads; network credentials and remote-file metadata are required for relevant operations.

features.name: Repository/image-host adapters
features.detail: GitHub, S.EE and Imgur have management/deletion clients; Lsky, Alist and other PicList servers have upload/deletion but no dedicated management client. Huawei OBS deletion depends on corresponding uploader records.

features.name: Browse actual remote assets
features.detail: Cloud manager selects account/bucket/repository/root and lists objects uploaded from any device, unlike machine-local gallery history.

features.name: Gallery/cloud grid and table views
features.detail: Thumbnail or row views, adjustable grid size, range selection, selected counts and per-file info.

features.name: Cloud pagination and all-page newest scan
features.detail: First/previous/next/last/jump navigation loads missing pages; + means unknown total. Newest scans all folder pages with cancellation; normal search/sort are page-scoped, and search stays page-scoped after newest scan.

features.name: Filename and recorded-URL search
features.detail: Gallery searches partial names or URL domain/path; cloud search scope is current page, not necessarily every remote file.

features.name: Gallery date/provider filtering
features.detail: Gallery filter controls narrow records by provider/date and sort order; history defaults newest first.

features.name: Multiple reusable link formats
features.detail: Copy Markdown/HTML/URL/UBB/custom links individually or in batches; gallery supports url/name/extension placeholders, cloud per-bucket templates also object path/directory.

features.name: External short-link service
features.detail: Long/short URL output is available but shortening requires a configured service; generated names or shortened URLs do not add privacy.

features.name: Provider-signed temporary links
features.detail: Cloud workflows support private temporary signed addresses and batch copying; expiration and accessibility depend on provider, not a PicList hosted share database.

features.name: Previewed bulk record URL replacement
features.detail: Select/filter records, inspect pattern-based before/after matches and final plan before applying. This edits history only, not remote filenames or published Markdown documents.

features.name: Cloud regex batch rename
features.detail: Cloud batch renaming/moving provides preview, conflict policies and failed-item retry; provider may implement rename via copy-then-delete and require both permissions.

features.name: Cloud downloads and folder transfer
features.detail: Downloads selected remote files/folders to chosen local path; transfer list supports pause/resume/cancel and per-item outcomes, with provider-specific paging constraints.

features.name: Separate history removal and remote deletion
features.detail: Delete from Cloud toggle decides whether gallery removal also deletes destination files. Adapters need stored uploader IDs, credentials and remote metadata; failed remote operations are reported.

features.name: Three-level image-processing inheritance
features.detail: Named configuration overrides provider overrides global defaults, including explicit disabled switches. Effective settings show value sources and can revert to inherited values.

features.name: Encoder-dependent quality control
features.detail: Quality presets/slider apply during upload; docs explicitly warn quality percentages are not guaranteed size savings and PNG may not shrink much.

features.name: Dimension/percentage resize and no enlargement
features.detail: Zero dimension preserves proportional sizing; percentage mode takes precedence over fixed dimensions, and small-image enlargement can be disabled.

features.name: Upload rotation/flipping
features.detail: Processing supports rotation and flips; these and later plugins may change final dimensions.

features.name: Input-specific format conversion
features.detail: Preserve source format or choose output with per-input-extension rules. Bypass extensions upload without processing; preview support does not establish encoder availability.

features.name: Text/image/tiled watermarks
features.detail: Text uses local/custom font, size/color/margins/position; image watermark supports scale/opacity/placement and full-image repeated coverage. Missing default-font download can skip watermark.

features.name: EXIF removal during processing
features.detail: Release specifically documents EXIF removal compatibility fixes for HEIF; complete preserved/removed field matrix is not established.

features.name: Date/hash/path naming templates
features.detail: Patterns support original basename, date/time/milliseconds, UUID/ULID, random fragments, MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256 and trailing local directories; extension is appended and nested paths depend on provider.

features.name: Paced upload queue
features.detail: Queue has pending/completed/failed states, reorder/priority, filename filtering, interval 0.1–99999 seconds, up to 10 auto retries, optional auto-start and pause-on-error.

features.name: Restart-aware queued uploads
features.detail: taskQueue.json persists state and identifies interrupted work; resume uses current default destination at execution time and requires original source paths.

features.name: Pause/cancel without undoing delivery
features.detail: Pause lets active file finish; cancel stops relevant pending work but does not remove delivered files. Cloud requests are cancelled when switching folders/accounts to avoid stale results.

features.name: Recover result saving without reupload
features.detail: Records remote completion separately from gallery/success-script finalization. Retrying original task uses persisted finalization data and API finalizationId rather than uploading again.

features.name: Private full-data backup workflow
features.detail: Documented backup closes app then copies configs, gallery DB, queue/recovery data and scripts; actual destination objects and outside fonts/dependencies need separate backup.

features.name: Configuration sync through Git/WebDAV
features.detail: Upload/download common settings, management settings or all configs using selected private Git/WebDAV target; direction can overwrite current defaults and contains credentials.

features.name: Previewed cross-device history sync
features.detail: Plans additions/updates/deletions/conflicts and supports local, remote or both conflict choices with exported summary; transfers records, never all cloud objects.

features.name: Scoped synchronization rollback snapshots
features.detail: Sync snapshots allow local rollback on failure with retention, size display, export/deletion and active-use protection. Cannot restore deleted remote objects; not general file-operation undo.

features.name: Image preview zoom/pan
features.detail: Scroll/+/− zoom, drag pan, reset, arrow navigation and Esc/close are documented.

features.name: SVG gallery preview
features.detail: v3.6 adds SVG image previews; non-image gallery entries use extension icons.

features.name: JPEG XL via PNG preview
features.detail: JXL can use generated PNG previews without changing stored original; JXL encoding support is not promised.

features.name: Cloud media preview
features.detail: Management media preview/playback depends on platform codecs, server response/range support; uploading arbitrary video files alone does not ensure playback.

features.name: Audio and text/code previews
features.detail: Management preview supports text/code and audio/media where runtime codecs and remote responses allow; unsupported content can be downloaded externally.

features.name: Local HTTP upload server
features.detail: Default endpoint is loopback port 36677/upload, with later port fallback; nonloopback callers need configured key query value, recognized loopback requests receive it automatically.

features.name: Markdown editor integrations
features.detail: Typora >=1.6 selects PicList directly; older Typora uses PicGo(app). Obsidian requires Image Auto Upload plugin and VS Code uses VS-PicList extension.

features.name: PicGo-compatible plugin ecosystem
features.detail: Many PicGo plugins work, not all. System npm is default; experimental bundled npm avoids separate installation but native plugins can still require build tools.

features.name: Managed JavaScript lifecycle scripts
features.detail: Scripts run at startup/shutdown, preprocess/transform/upload/success/gallery removal or manually; advanced uploader stage can set result URLs. Access includes filesystem/network and local .env values; no separate Node runtime required for scripting.

features.name: Companion Android configuration transfer
features.detail: PicHoro imports uploader configuration by QR code; codes can expose destination credentials and should be transferred privately.

features.name: Themes and mini/tray UI
features.detail: Built-in/custom themes/backgrounds, ThemeHub, mini drag/drop window and tray upload entry points, including Windows tray window in 3.6.

features.name: Former built-in web upload UI
features.detail: v3.6.1 removes old built-in webpage/web server; HTTP upload API and loopback preview cache are distinct and remain documented.

features.name: Companion Core container
features.detail: Docker runs separately maintained PicList-Core upload server; desktop repo has no Dockerfile/Compose and must not be presented as containerized gallery server.

limitations.text: Gallery history, configs and actual objects are independent; gallery sync/snapshots cannot restore deleted remote files or fix already published article links.
Queued destination is resolved when each task executes, not pinned on enqueue; changing defaults can redirect later files.
Cloud search normally covers current page, even after newest-files scans; newest order needs provider timestamps and can require loading all pages.
Provider upload/deletion/management capabilities differ and require their own permissions/settings. Temporary signed/cache URLs are not permanent public article links.
Configs, sync exports and QR codes can contain credentials. Scripts access files/network, clipboard monitoring can upload screenshots and default watermark fonts may be fetched online.
Exact/perceptual duplicate cleanup, face recognition, maps, full EXIF catalogue editing and E2EE are not established; hash naming is not duplicate detection.

gaps: No providers contacted with credentials or user files; throughput/codec support not benchmarked.
Live manuals may lead release; desktop/Core/mobile scope explicitly separated.
Encryption options mentioned for configuration sync were not sufficient to establish E2EE media storage.

R28.summary: Self-hosted visual bookmarking/image-board application centered on tagged pins and public/private boards, not a filesystem photo-library manager.
deployment: Docker images for AMD64, ARMv7 and ARMv8
Self-hosted Django backend and browser frontend
Separate browser extensions and CLI companion
R28.storage_model: Pins store source URL/referrer, description, owner and tags, referencing server-stored images with standard/thumbnail/square derivatives; boards have many-to-many pin membership. Docker persists SQLite database, media and settings under its mounted data directory, with optional PostgreSQL/MySQL configuration.
R28.privacy_model: Can be self-hosted with global login-only browsing and private pins/boards. Remote-image capture makes server HTTP requests to source sites; profile API includes Gravatar-related data. Owner/privacy checks are application controls, not evidence that static media URLs are encrypted or access-protected.
maturity_notes: Frozen commit 05476b112401cf34a38bfbffc67c37f5f6c3b38f; latest release v2.1.13 (2024-10-03), a small fix release.
Plugin system describes itself as a naive released implementation still under development.
README broadly mentions videos and webpages; inspected ingestion code validates images, so full video playback and arbitrary webpage archiving remain unclear.

features.name: Browser-based image boards
features.detail: Pinry's tiled pin/board interface is reached through the running instance's web address; browser extensions are separate capture companions.

features.name: Self-hosted Pinry server
features.detail: Official Docker guide runs a user-controlled server with a persistent data volume, database and local settings; alternate database backends can be configured.

features.name: Translated Pinry interface
features.detail: README explicitly lists implemented i18n support for English, Simplified Chinese and French in its application feature checklist.

features.name: Tiling visual pin board
features.detail: Browser interface presents saved image pins in a skim-friendly tiled board with online preview.

features.name: Fetch and retain remote images
features.detail: Creates pins from image URLs, optionally preserving referrer; server downloads content, verifies it is an image and creates local image/thumbnail records.

features.name: Upload images into pins
features.detail: Image creation endpoint accepts uploaded content; pin creation can reference image_by_id instead of fetching a URL.

features.name: Pin descriptions and source references
features.detail: Pins retain description, source URL and referrer in addition to publication time and submitting user.

features.name: Shared pin tagging
features.detail: Pins have multiple tags; serializer can create missing tags when assigned. Design distinguishes global tag classification from single-owner boards.

features.name: Owner-managed boards
features.detail: Boards have per-owner unique names and many-to-many pin membership, with pin counts and a cover derived from the first pin.

features.name: Filter pins by tags
features.detail: README and API expose tag-name pin filtering plus tag autocomplete; no semantic or image similarity search is established.

features.name: Find boards by name
features.detail: Board search uses name; autocomplete and owner-name filters help select boards.

features.name: Filter pins by owner or board
features.detail: API supports submitter username and board ID filters and lists pins/boards newest-first by ID.

features.name: Multiple accounts and signup control
features.detail: Multiuser application with configurable self-registration; Docker guide describes enabling new registrations in persisted local settings.

features.name: Owner editing and private content
features.detail: Object permission classes allow owner mutations and owner-only access to private pins/boards; list queries filter private records for nonowners and anonymous requests.

features.name: Public boards and pins
features.detail: Public/private booleans exist independently on pins and boards; public boards support sharing by board. This does not establish password/expiry-link support.

features.name: Disable anonymous browsing
features.detail: Example configuration has PUBLIC controlling whether pins are viewable without login, separate from per-object private flags.

features.name: Pre-generated display images
features.detail: Image ingestion generates standard, thumbnail and square derivatives; example sizes are 600-wide, 240-wide and cropped 125-square, configurable by IMAGE_SIZES.

features.name: Token-authenticated resource API
features.detail: User profile supplies a token; DRF exposes interactive API plus pin/board creation/editing and image upload. Board add/remove ID lists are capped at ten per update.

features.name: Chrome/Firefox capture extensions
features.detail: Official docs link a separately maintained browser-pinry extension and browser stores for adding web content.

features.name: Command-line pin submission
features.detail: README links pinry-cli-py companion for adding an image or URL; not a built-in executable in this repository.

features.name: Image-processing lifecycle hooks
features.detail: Configure Python plugin objects in ENABLED_PLUGINS; hooks run before image/thumbnail creation and can modify objects. Documentation offers watermarking as an example, not a ready-made watermark UI.

features.name: Backup persisted server data
features.detail: Docker guide instructs copying the mounted data directory containing database, settings and pins; no automatic scheduled backup/restore UI is claimed.

features.name: Delete associated pin media
features.detail: Deleting a pin triggers deletion of its image record; example settings enable image-file auto-deletion. This is cleanup, not recoverable trash.

features.name: Multi-architecture Docker distribution
features.detail: Published images cover ARMv7/ARMv8/AMD64 and persist all data via a mounted directory or named volume.

features.name: Choose catalogue database backend
features.detail: Docker defaults to SQLite for small personal deployments; guide documents switching local settings to PostgreSQL or MySQL.

features.name: Native saved-video playback
features.detail: README description includes videos but detailed feature list emphasizes images and URL ingestion explicitly validates image content; playback semantics/formats are not established.

features.name: Archive arbitrary webpage content
features.detail: README mentions webpages but model/API evidence establishes image URL, referrer and description rather than a full HTML capture/archive pipeline.

limitations.text: Board design is single-owner, not evidence of collaboratively editable multi-owner albums; private pin and board flags are separate.
Remote URL image creation is synchronous in the inspected model (asynchronous processing remains a TODO), and board membership patch lists allow at most ten IDs per list.
Private record filtering is not proof of protection of direct static-media URLs; no encryption, expiring links or media retention recovery was established.
No EXIF/GPS catalogue, duplicate detection, filesystem scan/watch, AI people or video playback implementation was established by the available docs/source.
Plugin API is early; available-plugin catalogue is blank/coming soon, so example watermarking should not be treated as a finished feature.

gaps: Image-centric implementation does not substantiate all broad README video/webpage wording.
No native photo-library AI, metadata or duplicate workflows established.
Static asset authorization was not audited; private flags are not a security guarantee.

R29.summary: Interactive local AI organizer that proposes content-derived names and category directories, then creates hard-linked views of files; not a photo catalogue or duplicate finder.
deployment: Python 3.12/Conda CLI on Windows, macOS and Linux
Nexa SDK with downloaded Llama 3.2 and LLaVA models
R29.storage_model: Recursively reads existing files. Current operation generation creates hard links in the selected output tree, rather than independent copies or moves. Original paths remain; linked paths share underlying data. Text operation logs are optional.
R29.privacy_model: Inference is local through Nexa SDK, without an AI API. Initial models/dependencies require downloads; main.py also invokes NLTK downloads at startup. The README's offline statement is therefore conditional on provisioning, not a guarantee of zero network access.
maturity_notes: Manifest pins a19559942a35d98e9d2168fa58f288d9ea294bc6; latest release new_version (v0.0.2), 2024-10-01; last repository push 2024-10-21.
README references multiprocessing, but the inspected main workflow explicitly processes image and text groups sequentially; no parallel-inference claim is made here.

sources.summary: Released dry preview, silent logging, new formats and three organization modes.

features.name: Interactive organization CLI
features.detail: Prompts for input/output paths and content, date or type organization; can retry a different mode or process another directory within the same session.

features.name: Recursive file discovery
features.detail: Accepts a directory or single file, recursively collects paths and excludes dot-prefixed filenames; hidden directory traversal is not explicitly excluded by os.walk.

features.name: Local text and vision inference
features.detail: Content mode initializes quantized Llama3.2-3B-Instruct q3_K_M and llava-v1.6-vicuna-7b q4_0 through Nexa; these models run on the user's machine.

features.name: Content descriptions for naming
features.detail: Text summaries and image descriptions drive suggested category folder names and filenames; not a persistent searchable caption catalogue.

features.name: AI-generated category directories
features.detail: Content analysis produces foldername and filename values used to construct the proposed output hierarchy.

features.name: Descriptive output filenames
features.detail: Generates descriptive names while preserving extensions; sanitizer removes unsuitable words/punctuation, lowercases, separates words with underscores and limits length to 50 characters/five words.

features.name: Modification-date folders
features.detail: Date mode creates year/month-name directories using filesystem modification time, not EXIF capture dates, and retains existing filenames.

features.name: Extension-based organization
features.detail: Type mode separates image_files, text_files with plain-text/document/PDF/spreadsheet/ebook subcategories, and others; this does not imply semantic ebook understanding.

features.name: Hard-linked output views
features.detail: All three planning modes currently assign hardlink, and execution calls os.link. Original filenames remain; output is not an independent backup and cross-filesystem creation can fail.

features.name: Preview proposed directory tree
features.detail: Shows the proposed hierarchy before executing operations and offers another organization mode when the proposal is rejected; execute_operations also has an explicit non-mutating dry_run path.

features.name: Confirmation before linking
features.detail: Output creation and execute_operations occur only after a yes/no confirmation in the main workflow.

features.name: Limited collision protection
features.detail: Content mode adds numeric suffixes for repeated proposed destinations in the current batch. Existing destinations cause os.link errors logged per operation rather than overwrite; date/type modes do not disambiguate duplicate basenames.

features.name: Silent text logging
features.detail: Silent mode appends messages and operation successes/failures to operation_log.txt; it is not a transactional journal or undo mechanism.

features.name: Progress and elapsed time
features.detail: CLI reports path-load time and execution uses a progress bar with elapsed time and per-operation advancement.

features.name: Document content extraction
features.detail: Readers handle UTF-8 text/Markdown, DOCX-style documents, PDF, Excel/CSV and PowerPoint text. Plain text is capped at 3,000 characters and PDF at its first three pages; legacy .doc/.ppt are routed through libraries primarily intended for modern formats, so successful legacy parsing is not guaranteed.

features.name: Raster image analysis
features.detail: README lists PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP; source additionally classifies TIFF as an image. This is analysis eligibility, not documented animated playback or RAW decoding.

features.name: No mandatory content upload
features.detail: The documented content-analysis workflow uses local models and requires no hosted AI API.

features.name: Provisioned local processing
features.detail: README documents processing without Internet once models are set up; startup calls NLTK download and missing Nexa models are downloaded, so completely disconnected first-run setup is not established.

features.name: Optional GPU-enabled SDK
features.detail: Installation documents a Metal build for macOS and links to Nexa CUDA/AMD support; CPU installation is also provided.

features.name: Conversational Copilot mode
features.detail: Roadmap proposes telling AI how to organize and rename files through conversation.

features.name: Model selection in CLI
features.detail: Changing models through the CLI is an unchecked roadmap item; current model identifiers are fixed in initialization source.

features.name: Duplicate detection
features.detail: Checking file duplication remains on the roadmap. Current processed-path and destination-name sets are not duplicate-content detection.

features.name: Audio, video and ebook understanding
features.detail: Semantic support for ebooks, audio and video is listed as future work; extension-only ebook placement is already present in type mode.

features.name: Docker distribution
features.detail: Dockerfile is explicitly unchecked in the roadmap.

features.name: Standalone desktop executables
features.detail: macOS/Linux/Windows executables are planned; currently documented installation requires Python, Conda and SDK dependencies.

features.name: Johnny Decimal organization
features.detail: Implementing established organization schemes such as Johnny Decimal is an unchecked roadmap item.

limitations.text: Translated or user-selectable UI languages are not established in the inspected README and interactive CLI source; this is a documentation gap, not an assertion that localization is unsupported.
Hard links share content and require filesystem support; editing a linked output can affect the original. Code logs link failures and has no documented copy fallback or rollback.
Offline inference does not imply zero-network startup: NLTK resources and missing model weights are downloaded.
Only limited document text is sampled; PDF reader extracts text rather than performing demonstrated OCR. Imported pytesseract alone does not establish an OCR feature.
Gallery browsing, EXIF editing, face recognition, maps, album sharing, catalogue search and recoverable trash are not established in the inspected documentation/source.

gaps: No separate user manual exists in the inspected tree; README, release and three complete implementation files establish the limited CLI scope.
Model accuracy and platform execution were not tested.

R30.summary: Local, tag-centric media archive with managed content-addressed storage, powerful download automation and unusually detailed duplicate-relationship workflows.
deployment: Windows installer or portable ZIP
Linux built archive or source installation
Official macOS client runs from source; separate third-party Hydra Vista macOS client
Optional bundled file/tag repository server, not a photo web UI
Optional third-party browser UIs such as Hydrus Web/Hydrui and Android clients such as hydit/aether, connected through the enabled Client API
R30.storage_model: Imports copies into hash-named managed storage using SHA-256 identity; original filenames/folders are not the catalogue model. Settings, tags, ratings, notes, URLs and relationships live in SQLite databases. Media/thumbnails may be distributed over weighted storage locations while the database stays local; local file domains are overlapping database subsets, not independent catalogues.
R30.privacy_model: Default operation is local with no sharing or phone-home according to project documentation. Downloads, tag/file repositories and Client API are explicit network integrations. Repository uploads can reveal identifying content and server operators see connection IPs; transport encryption is not E2EE. Deleting a file retains much of its metadata, and website login credentials are explicitly not securely stored.
maturity_notes: Frozen master commit c78a5cbe76e7b77a2f652187e8343907fa7f27ba; release v694a dated 2026-11-04.
Project targets frequent weekly releases and is chiefly solo-maintained; README says public pull requests are closed.
README/release explicitly urge users of v691 or older to update to v692+ for a disclosed remote-code-execution flaw; this profile is not a security audit.
macOS Intel application has been discontinued in current installation guide; source remains supported. Older examples still mention the legacy app.
Advanced alternate categorization and fully headless client operation remain incomplete/planned. Third-party plugins are not maintained or guaranteed by the hydrus author.
