features.name: Browser gallery and dashboard
features.detail: Visitors browse the web gallery and administrators sign in to /dashboard for uploads, albums and configuration; setup is also browser-based.

features.name: Persistent Docker deployment
features.detail: README recommends published Docker/Compose images with the data directory mounted for database, settings, session secret and local photos; this is a web-server deployment.

features.name: Dashboard language switching
features.detail: README explicitly lists dashboard language switching as an application feature. Exact supported interface-language list is not specified in the inspected source; separate place-name language settings and translated README files are not treated as UI-localization evidence.

features.name: Self-hosted browser gallery
features.detail: Admin/browser UI and public gallery run on an operator-controlled server; Docker image with persistent data mount is recommended.

features.name: Managed Cloud alternative
features.detail: README links a separate sign-up hosted service for creating galleries without maintaining a server; inspected material does not establish pricing or entitlement limits.

features.name: Browser-first setup and settings
features.detail: Wizard creates an administrator and chooses site/storage; everyday settings persist in database and can be changed without rebuilding containers or editing .env.

features.name: Batch and drag-and-drop uploads
features.detail: Dashboard photo page accepts selected/dropped batches, optionally targeted to an album; successfully processed photos join the selected album.

features.name: Skip duplicate upload while adding album membership
features.detail: When duplicate handling is Skip, an already existing photo is added to the chosen album without uploading another file. Documentation does not specify the identity algorithm.

features.name: Scan media already in storage
features.detail: Storage guide explicitly says directly copied/uploaded backend files do not appear automatically and scanning/importing existing storage is planned.

features.name: Masonry gallery
features.detail: Photo wall uses masonry presentation with filters/sorting; header can be embedded in the wall or fixed during scrolling.

features.name: Time-oriented browsing
features.detail: README explicitly supports browsing by time; v1.2 release preserves mobile date-range controls while redesigning the header.

features.name: WebGL large-image viewer
features.detail: Viewer provides pan/zoom and tiled rendering for large images, not merely a precomputed thumbnail grid.

features.name: Image histogram display
features.detail: README photo-browsing feature list explicitly includes histograms.

features.name: Mobile interaction and live playback
features.detail: Live/Motion assets play on hover or long press; v1.2 updates mobile gallery controls and accessible header behavior.

features.name: Customizable photo management table
features.detail: Admin table supports sorting/filtering, persistent visible-column choice, upload-date sorting and Shift-click range selection.

features.name: Create and reorder albums
features.detail: Organize albums and order photos inside them; batch Add to album skips items already in the target album.

features.name: Custom album slugs with redirects
features.detail: Self-hosted titles generate slugs; numeric links redirect to current slug and historical slugs temporarily redirect. Renaming title alone keeps URL; editing/clearing frees the old slug for reassignment.

features.name: Automatic EXIF extraction
features.detail: Upload queue extracts EXIF and shooting coordinates, generates previews and resolves locations.

features.name: Edit title and description
features.detail: Dashboard edits descriptive metadata; inspected guides do not establish embedded-file write-back.

features.name: Photo ratings
features.detail: Rating is explicitly editable alongside title and description in dashboard.

features.name: Remove photo location data
features.detail: Privacy setting automatically strips location from future uploads; existing photos require individual/batch removal jobs and queue-completion confirmation. This is not a claim to remove every identifying field.

features.name: HEIC/HEIF image ingestion
features.detail: Documented image inputs include HEIC/HEIF alongside JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF.

features.name: Filename-paired Apple Live Photos
features.detail: Matches image and MOV sharing basename; either upload order works and pairing can be retried in dashboard.

features.name: Embedded Motion Photo playback
features.detail: Supports embedded-video Motion Photos with hover/long-press playback; separate from image/MOV pair matching.

features.name: Configurable interactive map
features.detail: Choose MapLibre with built-in MapTiler data or Mapbox, requiring appropriate tokens unless a custom MapLibre style is supplied. Photos need existing GPS; enabling maps cannot invent coordinates.

features.name: City/country place-name lookup
features.detail: Mapbox or Nominatim performs reverse geocoding separately from browser tile rendering; configurable language affects future lookups, and existing names require reindexing.

features.name: Custom map and geocoder endpoints
features.detail: Custom MapLibre Style JSON can reference self-hosted tiles/fonts/sprites with browser CORS; Nominatim URL can target a self-hosted service/proxy. This is not a bundled offline basemap or geocoder.

features.name: Public gallery and scoped photo shares
features.detail: README includes share previews; photo shares retain album access scope. Hidden-album membership restricts anonymous photo access even when the same photo also belongs to a public album.

features.name: Password-protected albums
features.detail: Minimum six-character album password; visitors must unlock application access. External public image URLs remain outside this protection.

features.name: Configurable gallery reactions
features.detail: v1.2 release adds controls to disable gallery reactions; precise reaction types are not stated in inspected note.

features.name: Optional GitHub administrator login
features.detail: Email/password is established at setup; GitHub OAuth requires configured client credentials and returned email matching an existing administrator, not arbitrary GitHub-user admin access.

features.name: Original and batch downloads
features.detail: Public viewer offers original downloads and dashboard selection supports batch download; exact archive format is not established by inspected guide.

features.name: S3-compatible backends
features.detail: Supports endpoint/bucket/region/prefix/credentials/path-style/CDN URL configuration with examples for AWS S3, R2, OSS, COS and MinIO; browser direct uploads need CORS and multipart ETag exposure.

features.name: OpenList storage integration
features.detail: Uses OpenList API token/root and configurable upload/delete/metadata endpoints; remote permissions and expiring download URLs affect accessibility.

features.name: Manage multiple storage schemes
features.detail: Dashboard adds/edits/selects local, S3 and OpenList schemes. Changing active scheme affects new uploads only; this is not multiple independent user-selectable catalogues.

features.name: Separate image-serving CDN URLs
features.detail: Remote storage can provide a separate CDN read base URL; R2 S3 upload endpoint must not be confused with its public image domain.

features.name: Processing task queue
features.detail: EXIF, thumbnails, locations and Live Photo pairing run after uploads; dashboard reports task progress/errors and failed-task retries.

features.name: Batch reindex and repair
features.detail: Selected photos can be reindexed, location names rebuilt after language changes and Live Photo pairing retried without claiming a full user-data reset.

features.name: Live logs and recent activity
features.detail: Dashboard exposes task errors/retries, live logs and activity; logs are not documented as a crash-recovery file operation journal.

features.name: Documented whole-instance backup
features.detail: Update guide requires stopping container and backing up complete data, Compose, legacy environment and separately stored local/remote media. Rollback restores pre-upgrade database and files, not just an older image.

features.name: Startup database migrations
features.detail: Migrations run automatically; current runtime image has no shell/package manager, and older manual in-container migration instructions no longer apply.

features.name: Optional analytics scripts
features.detail: Dashboard accepts custom tracking scripts in head/body; operators control the added privacy implications.

limitations.text: Direct storage copying is not an ingestion path; scan/import of existing backend media is explicitly planned.
Changing storage does not migrate files. Keep old schemes/paths reachable and back up remote stores separately.
Public S3/OpenList/CDN links bypass album-password enforcement and caches are not revoked by password changes; guide recommends local storage for protected albums.
Hidden membership overrides anonymous access even through another public album; freed slugs may be reused and old links can then open a different album.
Location stripping at upload affects future files only; check older files, descriptions and tags separately. Map providers need credentials/network or separately provisioned custom infrastructure.
No face recognition, perceptual duplicate scan, mobile backup, application trash, operation journal or encryption guarantee was established.

gaps: Duplicate identity algorithm and fine-grained search fields are not specified in inspected user guides.
Cloud pricing/entitlements and arbitrary standalone-video playback were not established.
Offline map packs, AI and recoverable file operations are not documented.

R44.summary: Self-hosted, tag-centric photo server with local object/style/color/face analysis and photo-version grouping; several sharing/mobile/video ambitions remain explicitly future work.
deployment: Docker Compose server with browser UI
Android/iPhone companion clients requiring a server
Documented image-analysis benchmarks include Raspberry Pi 4
R44.storage_model: Mounts existing photo directories; database, thumbnails and derived caches are stored separately. PostgreSQL stores catalogue/users/tags; Redis provides locking and service state. Multiple private/shared libraries can coexist.
R44.privacy_model: Photo analysis executes on the self-hosted server rather than external image-classification APIs; country/city lookup uses bundled geographic datasets. Browser access and server authentication do not imply E2EE or an offline map basemap. Operator must back up originals/catalogue.
maturity_notes: Repository pinned 7d2674f0ebf7851788748d6000e72f082d3c7248, pushed 2026-10-28; latest tagged release remains v0.24.0 dated 2021-11-18.
README explicitly describes pre-1.0, incomplete development with potentially broken parts; do not infer abandonment from release age or production readiness from recent commits.
Official website combines available features with future-tense proposals; these are separated below. Documentation repository is pinned independently to 104cd498c2ca906576ccc0e4a84632e7de7834ff.

features.name: Self-hosted photo server
features.detail: Runs on a home/server host and exposes a browser interface to authenticated devices; Docker Compose is the recommended setup.

features.name: Compose deployment
features.detail: Prebuilt application image is configured with PostgreSQL/Redis and mounted photos; data persists outside containers.

features.name: Browser photo interface
features.detail: Web-based filtering and full-screen viewing work from logged-in desktop/tablet/mobile devices.

features.name: Android companion
features.detail: Official site links a Google Play client providing access to an existing server; it is not a standalone gallery or currently documented backup client.

features.name: iPhone companion

features.name: Existing photo directories
features.detail: Mount existing photo storage instead of copying into a proprietary container; database/thumbnails remain separate from originals.

features.name: Live directory monitoring
features.detail: Recursive inotify watches respond to completed writes, added files, directory additions, moves/renames and deletions. Per-LibraryPath watch_for_changes settings enable/disable watches.

features.name: Private and shared libraries
features.detail: Multiple libraries coexist in one installation and users switch through the account menu; CLI assigns accounts to libraries.

features.name: Multiple accounts
features.detail: Separate usernames/passwords support private user libraries and administrator-configured shared libraries.

features.name: Administrative commands
features.detail: create_library and create_user management commands provision additional accounts/library access; initial setup may use createsuperuser.

features.name: Full-screen photo viewer
features.detail: Viewer exposes camera/time metadata and analysis results by scrolling, including colors, objects and map location.

features.name: Camera-derived metadata
features.detail: Uses aperture, shutter speed, GPS and capture date/time as searchable information; source adds camera, lens, ISO and focal-length constraints.

features.name: User and generated tags
features.detail: User-assigned concepts coexist with camera-derived and automatically classified tags; multiple tags per photo enable combined filtering.

features.name: Tag query filtering
features.detail: Queries resolve tag IDs or case-insensitive tag-name substrings; multiple filters are applied to the photo queryset.

features.name: Technical shooting filters
features.detail: Supports camera/lens IDs, aperture/ISO/focal-length ranges, exposure values, flash and metering/drive/shooting modes.

features.name: Rating-range search
features.detail: rating filters apply an inclusive star-rating range; this proves filtering, not the location or format of rating writes.

features.name: Human-readable date filtering
features.detail: Parses month names/abbreviations, day ordinals and years into capture-date constraints; when a month lacks a year, selects the current or most recent applicable year.

features.name: Weighted color discovery
features.detail: A fixed color palette is compared with a 32x32 resampled image using weighted HSV distance; results retain sufficiently significant color proportions.

features.name: Object content tags
features.detail: Object classifier runs within Photonix, stores bounding boxes and uses detected area as a significance signal; models are not a hosted Google API.

features.name: Artistic style classifier
features.detail: Classifies style labels such as geometric, minimalist and noir, distinct from literal object labels.

features.name: Server-local classifiers
features.detail: Object/face/style/color and location analysis run inside the deployment; configuration enables/disables individual classifiers to manage CPU/RAM.

features.name: MTCNN facial regions
features.detail: MTCNN detects face boxes and landmarks, creating initially unknown location-specific face tags.

features.name: FaceNet identity matching
features.detail: Aligned face crops generate 128-value FaceNet embeddings; Euclidean similarity thresholds match identities across images.

features.name: Unknown-person groups
features.detail: Unmatched faces form conservatively grouped Unknown person tags during import. Annoy nearest-neighbor indexes rebuild at five-minute intervals when needed, with direct comparison for newly added faces.

features.name: Rename face groups
features.detail: Users label automatically grouped unknown people with names, allowing personalized recognition without training a full new face model.

features.name: Approve/reject/edit face labels
features.detail: UI shows bounding boxes and supports approval, rejection and editing automatic face tags; documentation describes merging groups as the preferred correction path.

features.name: Bundled country/city lookup
features.detail: Uses World Borders polygons and GeoNames top-1000 cities locally with no API calls; returns nearest city only within 10 km. Coarse coastlines may miss beach locations.

features.name: Photo location map
features.detail: Official feature overview documents viewing geographic location on a map; no offline tile-cache guarantee is inferred from offline geocoding.

features.name: Version-aware RAW/edit grouping
features.detail: Compares timestamps and other metadata to group camera RAW, camera JPEG and edited versions; latest inferred edit becomes the preview while other versions remain accessible. This is not exact hash deduplication.

features.name: Deferred classifier queues
features.detail: Disabling an analysis type stops processing but newly imported photos remain queued and are analyzed when it is re-enabled.

features.name: Separate thumbnail/cache storage
features.detail: Thumbnails and cache data are outside the originals' directory; v0.24.0 addresses corrupt-image thumbnail crashes.

features.name: Self-controlled image processing
features.detail: Mounted originals and local classifiers avoid mandatory third-party image upload; operating a remotely accessible server remains the user's responsibility.

features.name: Automatic camera-roll uploads
features.detail: Official mobile-app section explicitly says automatic camera-roll uploading is a feature to come; present apps provide server access.

features.name: External photo/album sharing
features.detail: Sharing-online section asks users to wait until the feature is fully ready; it must not be counted as existing public-link sharing.

features.name: Presentation and multi-screen slideshow
features.detail: Official site describes phone-controlled TV/client presentations as future work, not an available feature.

features.name: Video support
features.detail: Official site explicitly says limited video-file support is intended soon; current documented scope focuses on photography.

features.name: Manually select preferred edit
features.detail: Current grouping chooses the inferred latest edit; manually preferring an older edit is described as upcoming.

features.name: Account/library management UI
features.detail: User/library guide states management UI is yet to be developed and directs administrators to CLI provisioning.

features.name: Fine-grained library roles
features.detail: Website discusses read-only/read-write roles and invitations in future tense; inspected current user guide establishes membership but not all UI/permission workflows.

limitations.text: The inspected official feature overview, configuration guide and repository documentation do not establish translated UI or a language selector; locale-related tree discovery found no positive evidence, which is not proof of absence.
README explicitly warns that the project is not feature-complete for 1.0 and requires operator-managed backups.
Offline geocoding only considers a coarse country map and 1,000 major cities within 10 km; it is not complete street/address geocoding.
Available mobile apps require a server and do not establish camera-roll backup. Public sharing, presentations and video support are future-tense on the official site.

Exact content dedupe, destructive cleanup safety, metadata writeback/sidecars, end-to-end encryption and a guaranteed offline map are not established. Version grouping must not be recast as exact duplicate detection.

gaps: Official website has old/future-tense sections; planned and unclear entries are not treated as shipped functionality.
No runtime verification of recently changed master against the 2021 stable tag.

R45.summary: Server-side, folder-based photographic DAM emphasizing fast IPTC keyword retrieval, face/object assistance and basket-based export to desktop editing workflows.
deployment: Self-hosted web server
Docker, recommended/supported installation
64-bit standalone server binaries on Windows/Linux/macOS when published
Separate desktop clients for Windows, Linux and universal macOS
R45.storage_model: Indexes originals in a server directory tree; SQLite catalogue and derived thumbnails live in configurable volumes. Keywords are queued and written into originals by ExifTool without JPEG re-encoding. Desktop basket downloads mirror server paths; return synchronization is manual.
R45.privacy_model: Current README explicitly provides local/offline face detection and recognition, replacing legacy Azure Face API use. No mandatory external original upload is documented; WordPress publishing and desktop synchronization are explicit workflows. Authentication is disabled by default, granting anyone who can reach the server browsing/modification/download access. Map-provider offline behaviour and media encryption are not established.
maturity_notes: Frozen master commit e110926104cc93d3c87a9617ba7ab4ae70dbb216; latest release 4.5.3 dated 2026-01-14.
4.5.3 upgrades to .NET 10; README/FAQ retain older .NET 7 wording and some older installation examples.
Claims of sub-second search over 500,000 images and multi-day initial processing are author-reported, hardware-dependent observations, not benchmarks performed here.
Cropping/colour editing, deduplication, video and automatic desktop-to-server synchronization remain in README's planned section and are not counted as present.

features.name: Server-side photo catalogue
features.detail: Central server/library can be used from several devices without copying catalogue databases onto each client.

features.name: Browser frontend
features.detail: Web-based photo browsing, search, tagging and export UI with selectable themes.

features.name: Docker server
features.detail: Recommended supported deployment mounts pictures, config/database and thumbnails separately; default port is 6363.

features.name: Windows desktop client and server binaries
features.detail: README/FAQ document Windows standalone server and desktop client distributions; non-Docker server builds are not published for every release.

features.name: macOS desktop client and server binaries
features.detail: Universal macOS desktop client plus standalone server packages are documented, subject to release availability and dependency setup.

features.name: Linux desktop client and server binaries
features.detail: Linux standalone client/server packages supplement Docker; 64-bit OS is required.

features.name: Index originals in place
features.detail: At startup scans the configured photo tree and extracts metadata from existing originals; files need not be imported into a proprietary store.

features.name: Combine multiple mounted roots
features.detail: Server scans one top-level tree; documented Docker workaround mounts several shares/volumes as distinct subfolders beneath /pictures.

features.name: Folder-based library and desktop mirror
features.detail: Preserves server folder organization; desktop Save Locally copies basket images under the matching client-relative folder tree.

features.name: Automatically observe file changes
features.detail: Creates OS-level watchers per folder, automatically indexing added/updated images after the initial metadata pass.

features.name: Incremental background indexing
features.detail: After initial indexing, changes are processed without manually rebuilding the whole catalogue; initial metadata pass prioritizes recently modified files.

features.name: Exclude directories with .nomedia
features.detail: A .nomedia file in a folder causes that folder to be skipped by indexing; this is scan exclusion, not an encrypted vault.

features.name: Reorganize image files
features.detail: Move or copy images between folders through the application.

features.name: Trash-folder deletion
features.detail: README specifies image deletion through a trashcan folder; automatic retention duration and restoration guarantees are not documented in inspected manuals.

features.name: Thumbnail browsing and selection
features.detail: Thumbnail browser supports selection for keyword edits or basket addition, while individual images show properties and AI tags.

features.name: Date-grouped browsing
features.detail: README identifies browsing grouped by date and release 4.5.3 updates advanced date-range UI.

features.name: Full-text partial phrase search
features.detail: README explicitly supports full-text multi-phrase, partial-word retrieval; exact filename/path tokenization is not specified in the inspected feature section.

features.name: Keyword and untagged filtering
features.detail: Find by keyword tags and explicitly filter images with no keyword tags.

features.name: Technical metadata filters
features.detail: Advanced search filters camera/lens make/model and orientation.

features.name: Date interval selection
features.detail: Advanced search includes date ranges, with a redesigned date-range selector in release 4.5.3.

features.name: File-size filtering
features.detail: Advanced search explicitly lists file-size criteria.

features.name: Face and identity filters
features.detail: Search objects, detected faces and identified faces; anonymous face detection and named-person matching are distinct.

features.name: Find visually similar images
features.detail: README explicitly lists visual-similarity search. It does not establish exact hashes or duplicate-removal support.

features.name: Read photographic metadata
features.detail: Indexer extracts resolution, capture timestamp and EXIF metadata into the searchable catalogue.

features.name: Index IPTC keywords
features.detail: MetadataExtractor-based IPTC keyword indexing supports the documented tagging/search workflow.

features.name: Manage photographic keywords
features.detail: Add keywords to selected images, an entire basket or the current photo in the properties screen.

features.name: Batch keyword edits
features.detail: Selected images and basket contents can receive keyword operations together; pending additions/removals are combined in the background queue.

features.name: Write metadata back without recompression
features.detail: ExifTool applies queued keyword and other metadata operations to underlying originals without re-encoding JPEG image pixels. Originals are modified, so this is not read-only storage.

features.name: Resume pending metadata writes
features.detail: Pending metadata operations survive restart and are processed later; batching coalesces updates to reduce disk work.

features.name: Detect face regions
features.detail: Runs face detection after thumbnails are generated, using lower-resolution derived images for analysis.

features.name: Match people across photos
features.detail: Creates unknown people from distinctive face traits and matches future faces to the existing person; latest README says this now runs locally/offline.

features.name: Name unknown people
features.detail: Click a detected face to name its associated person; same-named different people need disambiguating names.

features.name: Merge split identity groups
features.detail: Assigning an existing name to another unknown person prompts a merge of face data, handling differences such as pose; split/reject workflows are not established here.

features.name: Object recognition and colour classification
features.detail: Recognized objects/faces appear as special icon-marked tags beside ordinary keywords; README also lists image-colour classification.

features.name: Local offline face processing
features.detail: Current README explicitly replaces formerly used Microsoft Azure Face API with local/offline detection and recognition; older Azure lineage must not be treated as a current requirement.

features.name: Scheduled and throttled AI work
features.detail: Set a processing time window and CPU throttling to limit intensive face/object jobs on shared NAS hardware.

features.name: Background thumbnail generation
features.detail: Generates browsing previews separately after metadata indexing and analyzes those thumbnails rather than originals.

features.name: Reuse Synology thumbnails
features.detail: SYNO_THUMBS uses Synology @eaDir layout so existing DSM thumbnails are reused and newly created ones can be used by Photo Station.

features.name: RAW preview/index support
features.detail: README lists DNG, CR2, ORF and NEF alongside JPG/PNG/TIFF/WebP/BMP; decoder support beyond these examples is not enumerated.

features.name: HEIC photos
features.detail: HEIC is explicitly included in supported formats and indexing description.

features.name: Map photos with geolocation
features.detail: Displays locations when image metadata provides them; offline basemap/geocoding or location-write support is not established.

features.name: Persistent image baskets
features.detail: Collect images from search results into reusable baskets for keywording, download/export or WordPress publication.

features.name: Private and shared baskets
features.detail: With authentication enabled users get a private My Basket and can expose a shared basket to all users. Without auth, anyone can alter any basket.

features.name: Optional user authentication
features.detail: Enable authentication in system settings and restart to obtain registered accounts, persistent user-associated baskets and user-tag operation attribution.

features.name: User, ReadOnly and Admin entitlements
features.detail: ReadOnly cannot modify keywords or download high-resolution images; User can; Admin manages settings/accounts. First user becomes admin and last admin cannot be demoted.

features.name: Basket download and local edit workflow
features.detail: Download/export basket images, including ZIP, or Save Locally in the desktop client to mirror server paths for external editing.

features.name: Export at chosen resolutions
features.detail: Basket export can generate files at different resolutions for publication/email; this is export processing, not a general in-place editor.

features.name: Watermark exports
features.detail: Exports optionally add watermarks for social/email use; standalone installation requires fonts for watermark rendering.

features.name: Publish to WordPress media library
features.detail: Basket images upload directly to a configured WordPress site; requires a separate WordPress JWT Authentication plugin and site/server credential setup.

features.name: General non-destructive photo edits
features.detail: README places cropping and colour adjustments in planned/in-progress enhancements, separate from existing lossless metadata and export processing.

features.name: Image deduplication
features.detail: README explicitly lists image de-duplication as in progress; existing visual-similarity search is not counted as duplicate cleanup.

features.name: Video support
features.detail: Roadmap says additional formats and possibly video; no current playback claim is made.

features.name: Automatic desktop-to-server synchronization
features.detail: Current workflow requires manually copying/rclone-syncing edits back; automatic return synchronization is explicitly future work.

features.name: Alamy stock-service upload
features.detail: README roadmap names selection/upload to Alamy; not established as available.

features.name: User audit reporting
features.detail: User IDs are associated with some operations, but the roles manual explicitly says audit reporting will come in a future release.

limitations.text: Authentication is off by default; anyone reaching the UI can browse, modify and download. Enabling authentication requires restart, and ReadOnly still permits browsing.
Initial thumbnails/AI can take days and saturate CPU on NAS hardware; time-window/throttling settings mitigate but do not eliminate processing costs. Watcher limits may need OS tuning.
Metadata writes modify originals, despite avoiding recompression; no sidecar-only mode, end-to-end encryption or durable reversible file-action journal is established.
Non-Docker setups are explicitly unsupported by the maintainer, need manually supplied dependencies and may lack binaries in a given release.
Same-named people must be disambiguated to avoid unintended identity merging. Face matches are not guaranteed across poses.
SQLite is current; PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB are only potential future alternatives in FAQ.
Offline map operation and translated interface language selection are not established by the inspected manuals or focused localization path discovery.

gaps: Old runtime/dependency wording conflicts with newer release; newest release takes precedence.
No exact duplicate algorithm, trash retention or offline map guarantee established; roadmap kept separate.

R46.summary: Legacy PHP/SQLite image host with guest uploads, direct/embed links, thumbnails, public discovery and optional externally processed compression/moderation.
deployment: Self-hosted PHP web application
PHP >=5.6 with PDO_SQLite, GD2, ImageMagick, fileinfo and pathinfo as documented
R46.storage_model: Local files and thumbnails are placed under year/month image directories; SQLite records retain upload and image details. Image identifiers use a 16-character slice of an MD5 digest. Deletion directly removes database records, originals and thumbnails.
R46.privacy_model: Local hosting is available but guest content is surfaced through discovery and public file URLs. Upload records store IP/user agent. Optional TinyPNG sends image bytes externally; ModerateContent receives a retrievable image URL. Authentication does not imply private albums or encryption.
maturity_notes: Manifest identifies archived/discontinued repository and directs new deployments to Zpic; frozen master b1f1b930e5860c2c1ce8e6d0e425b0ca79491d58.
Latest manifest release v2.31 is dated 2019-09-02; source was last pushed in 2022.
README advertises a separate ImgURL Pro edition. Its storage/MySQL/support claims are not attributed to this free repository.

features.name: Local PHP/SQLite hosting
features.detail: Host the site on a PHP server using SQLite 3 rather than the separate Pro edition's MySQL option.

features.name: Web upload and administration
features.detail: Browser upload, image detail, discovery and authenticated management pages are built in.

features.name: Batch and drag-and-drop upload
features.detail: README lists multi-image selection and drag-and-drop as current features.

features.name: Clipboard image upload
features.detail: Ctrl+V workflow sends base64 image content; parse endpoint validates MIME before storing it.

features.name: Remote URL image import
features.detail: Logged-in users can fetch supported image URLs; URL handler checks an image extension and rejects an already known digest-derived ID.

features.name: Year/month upload layout
features.detail: Original and thumbnail paths are created below imgs/YYYY/MM using generated digest-derived filenames.

features.name: Hash-derived duplicate upload handling
features.detail: Uses a truncated MD5 as image ID. URL/paste duplicates are rejected; multipart upload reuses the known record ID after writing/renaming the upload, so this is not guaranteed disk-level deduplication.

features.name: Web image upload formats
features.detail: Multipart allowlist includes GIF, JPG/JPEG, PNG, BMP and WebP. This evidence does not establish RAW or video playback.

features.name: Guest upload switch
features.detail: Admin settings enable/disable visitor uploads; uploads distinguish administrator versus visitor records.

features.name: Visitor daily quota and maximum size
features.detail: Configure guest daily upload count and backend file-size limit; upload constructor checks visitor IP quota. v2.31 fixes the size-setting bug.

features.name: Direct and embed link output
features.detail: UI/API can return URL, HTML, Markdown and BBCode; detail view exposes copy controls and direct download.

features.name: Upload and gallery JSON APIs
features.detail: Multipart upload returns IDs, paths, URL, thumbnail, dimensions and for newly inserted files a deletion URL; discovery API serializes gallery records.

features.name: Generated preview images
features.detail: Upload creates a 290×175 thumbnail where appropriate; small images can use the original URL instead.

features.name: Image cropping
features.detail: README explicitly lists image cropping alongside automatic thumbnail generation; crop variants and metadata preservation are not specified there.

features.name: Single/batch TinyPNG compression
features.detail: README lists batch compression; configured TinyPNG processing accepts JPEG/PNG, skips previously compressed records and overwrites the local original with downloaded output. Multiple configured API keys can be selected.

features.name: Optional external content review
features.detail: ModerateContent classifies a public image URL and stores the rating; already classified images are skipped, and batch helper selects up to five unknown entries. This is not local inference or face recognition.

features.name: Public discovery categories
features.detail: Discovery controller provides all, GIF, views and large-image categories; category query semantics beyond those labels are not inferred.

features.name: Paged gallery and administration
features.detail: Uses 16-image pages; public discovery caps the pagination count at 160 entries, while management has its own filters and count.

features.name: Upload-date administration filter
features.detail: Management accepts a start/end date and applies it to upload timestamps, separately for all, administrator or visitor records—not EXIF capture dates.

features.name: Find uploads by ID or IP
features.detail: Management can query numeric ID, 16-character image ID or uploading IP, and filter suspicious/adult-classified records.

features.name: Technical image detail display
features.detail: Image page lists dimensions, MIME, extension, upload time, file size and view count; EXIF capture metadata editing is not established.

features.name: Per-image viewing statistics
features.detail: Detail page displays stored view count and discovery offers a views category.

features.name: Upload provenance records
features.detail: Stores uploader IP, user agent, date, admin/visitor type, original client filename and moderation status.

features.name: Delete by private token link
features.detail: A valid deletion token authorizes removal without logging in; separate ID-based deletion requires login and both remove original, thumbnail and database entries.

features.name: Custom comment embedding
features.detail: Image view includes a comment.html file if present; this is an integration hook, not evidence of a built-in comment database.

features.name: Free-edition external storage roadmap
features.detail: Free README leaves external storage unchecked and free navigation only activates localhost. Pro's advertised support is separately classified.

features.name: Pro external storage and MySQL
features.detail: README advertises multiple external storage backends, MySQL, no advertising and professional support in separate ImgURL Pro; these are not verified free-source features.

features.name: Online updating availability
features.detail: README marks online update unfinished, but source navigation exposes a version-upgrade page. Its completeness was not established; not counted as present.

limitations.text: Focused localization review found no explicit multiple-language UI in the inspected README or image-host views/controllers. Framework language helpers are not evidence that the ImgURL user interface itself is localized.
WebP uploads explicitly record width/height as zero in the inspected handler; URL import's extension switch is narrower than multipart's WebP-capable allowlist.
Compression overwrites originals and deletion unlinks original/thumbnail files directly; no recycle/recovery layer is present in those inspected operations.
Digest-derived ID reuse is not proof of byte equality, and multipart duplicate detection occurs after files have been written; storage deduplication guarantees cannot be inferred.
Free external storage remains a roadmap checkbox, not the paid edition's available integration. Public discovery exposes only a bounded navigation window, not a complete large-library catalogue.
No inspected evidence establishes face/semantic search, EXIF editing, maps, collaborative albums, private per-user libraries, encrypted storage or reversible operation history.

gaps: No dedicated pinned manual exists in the source tree; multiple complete implementation files replace reliance on old external documentation.
Paid Pro announcement is documented separately, not audited as an available free feature.
External service availability and legacy PHP deployment compatibility were not runtime-tested.

R47.summary: Self-hosted image-upload and sharing platform centered on individually controlled image/collection links, hierarchical tags and configurable storage/authentication.
deployment: Self-hosted Docker/container web application with Symfony backend and SvelteKit frontend
R47.storage_model: Managed uploads with local storage by default, optionally SMB or S3-compatible storage. Local/SMB use separate images and cache directories; S3 stores image objects at bucket root and transformed variants under cache. HEIC/TIFF uploads are converted to JPEG rather than preserved in their original format.
R47.privacy_model: Private-by-default share records with publication/password/expiry gates, not E2EE. UI Copy Link publishes immediately and collections auto-publish on creation; guest uploads are public. EXIF stripping defaults on. Remote storage and OIDC are optional external dependencies. Documentation recommends proxy HTTPS/rate limiting and non-root containers.
maturity_notes: Manifest release v1.14.6 (2026-11-06); README pinned to aefc97065c20c543299d23b7315551c979705378.
Official live documentation inspected 2026-11-09 can be ahead of the pinned release; detailed controls are labeled as documented, not runtime-verified.
New share model migrates legacy links automatically except customized transformation links, which require recreation.

features.name: Browser image-sharing application
features.detail: Slink provides its upload, collections, share management and administrative interface through its SvelteKit web frontend backed by Symfony; Docker hosts the service and does not imply native desktop/mobile application builds.

features.name: Parallel multi-file image uploads
features.detail: README explicitly supports uploading multiple image files in parallel, with progress tracking and error handling for each file.

features.name: Nine documented UI languages
features.detail: README and introduction explicitly list English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Ukrainian and Chinese user interfaces. This is interface localization, not a claim about search-language or model support.

features.name: Self-hosted web image host
features.detail: Symfony/SvelteKit server with browser upload, management and sharing; container settings and persistent mounts are documented.

features.name: Container deployment and persistence
features.detail: Environment variables configure Docker/Compose deployments; local images require a host mount at /app/slink/images for persistence.

features.name: Explicitly published image shares
features.detail: Programmatically created shares start unpublished; UI Copy Link creates/reuses and publishes atomically. Unpublishing returns 404; holding a URL alone is insufficient if its share is revoked.

features.name: Password-gated shares
features.detail: Each share can set/change/remove a password; stored password is hashed and successful unlock creates a short-lived cookie.

features.name: Automatic share expiry
features.detail: Expiry timestamp can be set or cleared; passing it auto-revokes access.

features.name: Unified share management
features.detail: /shares lists owned image and collection shares; filters type, expired/has/no-expiry and password protection, with free-text underlying-name search.

features.name: Configurable URL shortening
features.detail: Shortening is enabled by default; generated code length defaults to 8 and is clamped between 4 and 32 characters.

features.name: Shareable collections
features.detail: Group images into a collection and share via one link; collection shares auto-publish upon creation, unlike API-created image shares.

features.name: Require accounts to view shares
features.detail: Instance settings separately require sign-in for media shares or collection shares; anonymous access to public routes is independently configurable.

features.name: Public Explore view
features.detail: Explore shows images users have made publicly visible; admin may disallow unauthenticated public-route access or force uploads public.

features.name: Concurrent multi-image upload
features.detail: Parallel multi-file upload tracks progress and per-file errors; maximum image size is configurable and chunk size defaults to 2 MB within a 1–25 MB range.

features.name: Opt-in anonymous uploads
features.detail: Disabled by default and admin-enabled; guests use drag/drop or file selection, uploads are public, and guests cannot edit/delete submitted images.

features.name: Upload duplicate detection
features.detail: Detects duplicate images during upload and notifies the user; enabled by default. Inspected docs do not specify hash/perceptual algorithm or a batch cleanup tool.

features.name: Upload image compression
features.detail: JPEG compression quality is configurable from 1 to 100, default 80.

features.name: Forced output format
features.detail: Optional setting converts all uploads to WebP, AVIF or JPEG; animated conversion is separately opt-in and disabled by default.

features.name: Strip uploaded EXIF
features.detail: IMAGE_STRIP_EXIF_METADATA defaults true; administrators can override at runtime. No preservation of untouched original metadata is implied.

features.name: HEIC ingestion with JPEG conversion
features.detail: HEIC and TIFF are accepted but converted to JPG before saving for compatibility.

features.name: AVIF upload and output
features.detail: AVIF is a supported upload format and configurable conversion target.

features.name: SVG and other image uploads
features.detail: Supported list includes SVG, BMP, ICO, PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF; broad image support is not evidence of video support.

features.name: Nested tags
features.detail: Hierarchical tag management has a dedicated management page and tag search capabilities.

features.name: Tag-based discovery
features.detail: README explicitly couples nested tags with search; arbitrary boolean/saved-query semantics are not documented.

features.name: Upload-history grid and list
features.detail: Upload history offers list/grid views of the user's uploads.

features.name: Bookmark public images
features.detail: Users save public images for later access; distinguished from changing ownership or copying originals.

features.name: Discussion on public images
features.detail: Users can leave comments on publicly visible images.

features.name: Interaction notifications
features.detail: Notifies users of interactions with their images; specific delivery channels are not established.

features.name: Light and dark interface modes
features.detail: README explicitly supports both light and dark application modes; interface translation is inventoried separately under deployment.localization.

features.name: Accounts and approval
features.detail: Email/password registration and login with configurable signup and admin approval; default environment reference requires approval before sign-in.

features.name: OIDC identity-provider login
features.detail: Google/Authentik/Keycloak/Authelia/Pocket ID presets or custom OIDC; matches sub then verified email, uses S256 PKCE, and stores client configuration encrypted.

features.name: Per-provider registration/approval overrides
features.detail: OIDC providers can inherit/allow/block registration and inherit/require/auto-approve new accounts independently of global signup policy; existing users are unaffected.

features.name: External upload API
features.detail: Bearer-authenticated POST /api/external/upload accepts multipart images and returns URL/metadata; login-protected endpoint exports ShareX config.

features.name: Named expiring API keys
features.detail: Keys have optional expiry, are displayed once and can be revoked; docs warn they permit uploads on the user's behalf.

features.name: ShareX uploader configuration
features.detail: Slink generates a .sxcu configuration for the separately installed ShareX client to automate screenshot uploads with an API key.

features.name: SMB/CIFS image storage
features.detail: Configured network share credentials store originals and transformed caches in automatically created slink/images and slink/cache directories.

features.name: S3 and compatible providers
features.detail: Supports AWS or custom endpoint/path-style S3 storage; AWS can use instance IAM role instead of static keys, but role mode is ignored for custom providers.

features.name: Transformed image cache
features.detail: Storage layouts separate uploaded images from transformed/cache objects locally, on SMB and under the S3 cache prefix.

features.name: Administrative statistics
features.detail: Admin dashboard provides statistics/analytics and storage-consumption metrics; documentation does not substantiate throughput benchmarks.

features.name: Administrative image moderation
features.detail: Administrators manage image content/visibility, users, storage and settings; stored settings override corresponding environment variables.

features.name: Built-in brute-force/rate protection
features.detail: Security guide explicitly says built-in rate limiting and brute-force protection are absent and recommends a reverse proxy for them.

limitations.text: No built-in rate limiting or brute-force protection; container runs as root by default. Guide recommends reverse proxy HTTPS/rate limiting and non-root configuration.
Guest uploads are public and cannot be edited/deleted by their guest uploader; docs recommend trusted/private environments due to content/moderation risks.
Copy Link publishes image shares immediately and collection shares auto-publish; private-by-default wording does not mean copied links stay inaccessible.
Legacy custom transformation shares are not auto-migrated. HEIC/TIFF are converted before storage, so this is not guaranteed untouched-original archival.
Deduplication algorithm, photo recognition, full video library, existing-folder scan, trash/undo and E2EE were not established by inspected sources.

gaps: Live manual may lead manifest release; no runtime validation performed.
README's upcoming-features link no longer exposed a roadmap in inspected introduction, so no roadmap features were invented.
Image transform parameter API beyond conversion settings was not established.

R48.summary: Local EXIF-driven file organizer and metadata-repair CLI that names photos/videos/audio by date, place and album, tracks checksums and can verify a stored library.
deployment: Python CLI with external ExifTool on macOS, Linux and Windows
Legacy experimental Electron taskbar GUI documentation
R48.storage_model: Organizes ordinary folders/files and embedded metadata rather than a proprietary media catalogue. It nevertheless maintains JSON checksum and location caches under its application directory (default .elodie), plus plugin JSON state; these are not a thumbnail browser catalogue.
R48.privacy_model: Core file/metadata work is local. Current default geolocation uses installed ExifTool geolocation database; configuring deprecated MapQuest invokes its network geocoding service. Optional Google Photos plugin uploads media to Google using OAuth. External automation/watch tools are separate.
maturity_notes: Frozen commit 4494ff851451a6b8d2c68562c05968791bf5ad40; manifest records no latest release.
Current README deprecates MapQuest in favor of ExifTool 13.13+ while sample config still shows a MapQuest key.
Legacy GUI guide uses Electron 0.34.2/Node 5.1.0 examples and calls itself a work in progress; current distributed GUI availability is not established.
Source inspection found dry-run initialization side effects and a trash-after-skipped-import caveat; no code was executed.

features.name: Scriptable file organization
features.detail: Commands import, update, generate-db, verify and batch operate on explicit files/directories with debug output.

features.name: Copy files into an organized library
features.detail: Import accepts one/multiple source files/directories and a destination, preserving source placement by default and using embedded metadata to choose paths.

features.name: Date/place/album folder templates
features.detail: Configurable folder placeholders include strftime date parts, city/state/country, camera make/model and album, with compound variables and ordered fallback choices.

features.name: Metadata-derived file naming
features.detail: Filename templates combine capture timestamp, original name, title/album and extension, remove missing placeholders and allow lowercase/default or uppercase output.

features.name: Photo EXIF capture/GPS extraction
features.detail: Prefers DateTimeOriginal/CreateDate/ModifyDate then filesystem times; GPS and camera metadata drive folder naming. Missing location goes to a configurable fallback.

features.name: XMP and QuickTime metadata
features.detail: Uses XMP title/album/GPS and QuickTime/H264 timestamps for video/audio; README distinguishes photo Title from video/audio DisplayName and read-only Composite GPS.

features.name: Update embedded metadata and reorganize
features.detail: update changes album, title, capture time or location through ExifTool and recalculates filenames/folders; it changes real files rather than only catalogue fields.

features.name: Set missing or incorrect capture times
features.detail: Import/update accept date or date-time overrides; import override replaces existing timestamp data, not merely fills missing values.

features.name: Assign GPS using a place name
features.detail: Import/update location names are resolved to coordinates and written into supported media metadata; supplied import location overwrites existing location.

features.name: Use source folder as embedded album
features.detail: --album-from-folder derives album metadata from input folders and template fallbacks can prioritize album over place; this is file organization, not virtual shared albums.

features.name: ExifTool local place lookup
features.detail: With ExifTool 13.13+ geolocation database, current default derives city/region/country from coordinates and resolves names without a MapQuest key. Availability is tested against installed ExifTool database.

features.name: Legacy MapQuest geocoding
features.detail: When a MapQuest key exists, name/coordinate lookups still call its API; README marks this deprecated and intended for removal, with optional English names.

features.name: Reuse previously resolved places
features.detail: Location lookup caches results in JSON and reuses a nearby cached location within a requested 3 km radius, reducing repeated lookups but potentially coarsening naming.

features.name: Skip previously imported content
features.detail: Computes SHA-256 and skips an existing matching stored path; if cache says a match but that file is missing, import proceeds. --allow-duplicates overrides normal skipping.

features.name: SHA-256 content identity
features.detail: Reads complete files in 64 KiB blocks into SHA-256 and maps hash to stored path; no perceptual similarity or byte-by-byte postverification is established.

features.name: Persistent checksum database
features.detail: hash.json retains signatures and locations between runs; a hash maps to one recorded path rather than a full duplicate group catalogue.

features.name: Regex import exclusions
features.detail: Repeated --exclude-regex switches and named config exclusions skip matching file/folder paths, including examples for NAS artifacts and thumbnails.

features.name: Preview imports, updates and plugin batches
features.detail: --dry-run reports file/metadata/plugin actions instead of media mutation; code guards hash/location writes. It is not a completely no-write process because directory/cache initialization can still occur.

features.name: Optional source-file trash after import
features.detail: --trash calls send2trash on original sources. Important source caveat: this call is not conditional on process_file returning a successful destination, so a skipped import can still trigger source trash.

features.name: Verify stored checksum baseline
features.detail: verify iterates hash/path records, reports missing files and recomputes content hashes to flag mismatches; it detects problems but does not repair corrupted files.

features.name: Regenerate checksum inventory
features.detail: generate-db --source rebuilds hash.json for an existing library; resetting a baseline differs from verifying the old baseline.

features.name: Timestamped checksum-cache backups
features.detail: Storage implementation provides timestamped copies of existing hash.json; this is backup of small integrity metadata, not copies of all media.

features.name: Import lifecycle and batch plugins
features.detail: Configured plugins expose before/after/batch hooks, JSON state and logging; a failing before-hook can prevent import.

features.name: Google Photos upload plugin
features.detail: Bundled optional plugin queues imported photos for Google upload via batch, requiring a Google API project, OAuth client and stored credentials. Guide is legacy and current Google API compatibility was not independently established.

features.name: Automated import triggers
features.detail: README explicitly relies on external inotify/cron/Automator/Hazel to invoke CLI when media arrives; Elodie itself is not documented as a persistent watcher.

features.name: HEIC metadata organization
features.detail: README requires ExifTool 11.50+ for HEIC support; this proves organization/metadata handling, not image decoding or playback.

features.name: Organize camera RAW, video and audio files
features.detail: README explicitly includes DNG/NEF and common video/audio alongside JPEG, with media-specific metadata precedence; no built-in playback is implied.

features.name: Taskbar drag-and-drop album edits
features.detail: GUI guide describes dragging Finder photos to create an album that writes EXIF and moves files, but calls the GUI unfinished and uses obsolete build tooling; manifest has no current release.

limitations.text: Location/time import overrides replace existing metadata. Metadata updates also relocate/rename files, so retain independent backups.
Source inspection shows --trash runs even when process_file returns no destination; users should not equate this switch with verified-copy-before-delete.
Dry run avoids media operations but initialization may create directories/empty state files; it is not a guaranteed zero-filesystem-write sandbox.
Although marketed without a proprietary database, implementation keeps JSON hash/location/plugin state; integrity checks require that baseline and only cover stored records.
No collision-safe overwrite guarantee, copy-content verification, recoverable operation journal, modern GUI release or perceptual deduplication was established.
MapQuest is deprecated but still invoked when configured; legacy Google Photos OAuth guide does not establish compatibility with current service restrictions.

gaps: Legacy GUI and Google plugin current operability are unverified.
Format support means metadata/file handling, not browser-style rendering.
Source-derived safety caveats were inspected, not executed or benchmarked.

R49.summary: Newsroom image asset-management platform centered on searchable editorial metadata, licensing/restrictions, publication usage and derivative crop distribution, with optional AWS-backed AI search.
deployment: Self-hosted multi-service Scala/Play system with Kahuna browser UI
Elasticsearch plus AWS S3, DynamoDB and messaging infrastructure
Local development uses LocalStack, but AI embedding still calls real AWS services
R49.storage_model: Uploads originals into managed object storage and generates thumbnail/optimized derivatives. Extracted and edited metadata/search projections live in database/search services; collections and publication usage have separate services. Crop exports are separately stored derivatives with requester/time provenance.
R49.privacy_model: Server-managed organizational asset store, not E2EE. User/machine authentication and API-key tiers gate access. Optional AI sends image/query inputs to AWS Bedrock and stores vectors in AWS services, including when a developer uses LocalStack. Production rights providers and authentication can depend on organization-specific external systems.
maturity_notes: Pinned main b874a49bc0ca091ad5762bf8b09a7ac457cbeaaa; manifest has no latest tagged release.
Documentation includes legacy ecosystem references and a provider-auth page explicitly marked work-in-progress; current source/tests are used to establish implemented permissions.
Vision document is aspirational and is not treated as proof of all goals. No throughput/latency benchmarks were run.

features.name: Kahuna image management UI
features.detail: Browser frontend accesses the microservices via hypermedia APIs; intended for organizational/editorial image workflows.

features.name: Self-hosted service suite
features.detail: Runs separately deployable services with Elasticsearch and AWS infrastructure; local setup provisions LocalStack resources.

features.name: Managed object storage
features.detail: Requires S3 buckets and DynamoDB resources; originals and derivative images are server-managed rather than a local folder browser.

features.name: Hypermedia service APIs
features.detail: APIs cover image ingestion/search, metadata, exports, collections, usage and auth; internal, readonly and syndication machine keys have distinct scopes.

features.name: Managed image upload
features.detail: Upload service prepares presigned uploads, accepts images with uploader/identifiers/timestamps/filename and exposes per-image/per-user upload status.

features.name: Derivative provenance ingestion
features.detail: Loader exposes enqueueDerivativeImage with derivativeOfMediaIds, preserving an explicit relationship to source assets.

features.name: Original and crop downloads
features.detail: Media API supplies original-file download and width-specific crop-export downloads; crop links are configurable.

features.name: Editorial field search
features.detail: Structured fields include title, description, copyright, credit, supplier reference, source, photographer/byline, category, subject, people-in-image, photoshoot and cropper identity.

features.name: Filename field search
features.detail: Query parser explicitly supports filename; this is managed-asset metadata search rather than browsing filesystem paths.

features.name: Structured filters and negation
features.detail: Supports field:value, quoted phrases, leading '-' negation, has:/is: conditions, # labels, collection: hierarchy terms and nested usages@field filters.

features.name: Capture/upload/date range search
features.detail: Distinguishes taken, uploaded/date and added dates; supports comparison operators, today/yesterday, multiple date formats and API since/until relative durations.

features.name: JPEG/PNG/TIFF filters
features.detail: fileType parser normalizes jpg/jpeg and tif/tiff plus png to MIME constraints.

features.name: Editorial location fields
features.detail: Searches location/city/state/country; the in alias expands across these descriptive fields. This is not a map or reverse-geocoding claim.

features.name: People-in-image metadata
features.detail: person query aliases peopleInImage metadata; no automatic facial recognition is implied.

features.name: Search by downstream usage
features.detail: Nested usages constraints include status, platform, section, publication, orderedBy and content references; request filters also cover usage and syndication status.

features.name: Paged search API
features.detail: Search provides offset/length and configurable orderBy; documented defaults are ten results ordered newest upload first.

features.name: Hybrid semantic/text ranking
features.detail: useAISearch plus enabled server configuration embeds query text through Bedrock and combines vector/text ranking; default vector weight is 0.85 and metadata/usage filters constrain the candidate pool.

features.name: Embedding-based image similarity
features.detail: AI similar:imageId uses the accessible source image's Cohere Embed v4 image vector for filtered nearest-neighbor retrieval. Missing vectors yield no results; combining image and text ranking signals is rejected.

features.name: AWS Bedrock embeddings
features.detail: Lambda sends images to real Bedrock and stores vectors in S3 Vectors even in LocalStack development; query embedding calls are likewise remote.

features.name: Shared in-flight query cache
features.detail: AI-search controller caches normalized query embeddings/futures so simultaneous equivalent queries share a remote call; zero-length polling skips Bedrock/KNN work.

features.name: Queued embedding/backfill
features.detail: SQS-fed embedding work supports retries/dead-letter behavior; documented backfill selects unembedded, non-soft-deleted assets.

features.name: Source IPTC extraction
features.detail: Ingestion extracts IPTC into source metadata and maps key fields into editable/searchable primary metadata.

features.name: Source XMP extraction
features.detail: Ingestion preserves source XMP metadata in the database before configurable classification/cleaning.

features.name: Custom searchable metadata schema
features.detail: Configuration defines collapsible domain sections with string/integer/datetime/select fields, controlled vocabularies, validation and searchable aliases without modifying application code.

features.name: Multi-image metadata editing
features.detail: Selected images show common values or Multiple values; saving applies per-image updates. Opt-in string edit modes support overwrite, prefix or suffix against each existing value.

features.name: Editorial licensing and restrictions
features.detail: Displays/edits usage categories, agency suppliers, publications/creators and required restriction text; unknown rights are explicit and some categories force restrictions.

features.name: Cost and allowed-use summaries
features.detail: Configured UI can show payable, all-use, news/sport eligibility and supplier markers, based on deployment-specific rights rules rather than generic image availability.

features.name: Metadata-template rights preview
features.detail: Configured templates preview their replacement usage-rights category in a locked editor and allow applying or cancelling without prematurely changing existing rights.

features.name: Ordered ingest processors
features.detail: ImageProcessor/MetadataCleaner interfaces enable configured Scala pipelines for agency detection, license assignment, credits and house-style normalization; custom implementations require integration, not a generic AI model.

features.name: Organization-specific rights sources
features.detail: Includes Guardian hardcoded and runtime-configured providers for photographer/illustrator lists and Creative Commons options; additional sources can implement the provider trait.

features.name: Hierarchical collections
features.detail: Collections have root/child/grandchild hierarchy. Root creation currently requires the API, not Kahuna UI.

features.name: Validated derivative crops
features.detail: Cropper verifies source ownership URI, image validity and bounds using oriented dimensions, then generates/stores crop exports separately from originals.

features.name: Derivative sizes and optimized download
features.detail: Crop creation yields master/additional sizings; optimized download API accepts width, height and quality parameters.

features.name: Separate crop derivatives
features.detail: Crop exports refer to a source image, have separate asset/download records and can be removed via crop permissions without a source rewrite in the inspected controller.

features.name: Crop requester and timestamp
features.detail: Each generated crop records authenticated identity, request time and specification. This is derivative provenance, not a durable crash-recovery file-action journal.

features.name: TIFF original and previews
features.detail: Uploads original TIFF and creates mandatory JPEG thumbnails plus optional optimized PNG; layered TIFF handling picks the extracted first image/layer for the preview rather than providing a complete multipage viewer.

features.name: Print/digital usage tracking
features.detail: Usage records connect images to articles/editorial systems or print issue/page/layout/publication details, with pending/published/removed state resolution.

features.name: Supplier usage/quota API
features.detail: Current API exposes supplier usage, image usage and quota-count/quota-for-image endpoints for contractual accounting.

features.name: Date histogram API
features.detail: Aggregation endpoint computes a date histogram for a chosen field and optional query.

features.name: Permission-gated editing/actions
features.detail: Rights tests specify edit permission or ownership; crop deletion uses a dedicated permission. Machine API tiers are internal, readonly or syndication-specific.

features.name: Partner syndication API
features.detail: Media API exposes per-partner image syndication and search can filter syndication status; downstream commercial integrations are deployment-specific.

features.name: Soft deletion and undelete API
features.detail: Current routes distinguish soft-deleted metadata, ordinary delete, explicit hard-delete and undelete. Retention period and complete recovery semantics are not documented by these routes.

features.name: Replica restoration endpoint
features.detail: Loader exposes images/restore calling restoreFromReplica; exact operator workflow/backup completeness remains unverified.

features.name: Resumable mass deletion utility
features.detail: Administrator script consumes image IDs and Internal API credentials, records last processed ID and separate success/error lists. Documentation explicitly says no mass-deletion UI; logs are not an atomic pre-operation journal.

limitations.text: Translated Kahuna UI or selectable interface languages are not established by the inspected primary documentation/source. Multilingual query characters and a service MessageTranslator are not treated as UI localization evidence.
AWS infrastructure is a documented dependency. Optional embedding calls real Bedrock/S3 Vectors even under LocalStack, so this is not guaranteed local/offline AI.
Collection roots require API creation; mass deletion uses a separate script rather than the UI.
Domain field removal drops editable/persisted values on updates; changing types may break old values, and aliases can collide with built-in query prefixes.
AI search cannot combine similar-image and textual ranking in one query, requires existing embeddings for image search and uses a configured result limit rather than ordinary unlimited paging.

Mobile backup, local-folder browsing, RAW development, face recognition, geographic maps, duplicate cleanup, E2EE and crash-recovery file journals are not established. person search is metadata, not facial identification.

gaps: No tagged release metadata; pinned main mixes active source and some older service docs.
API-only recovery/quota endpoints are medium-confidence capability evidence; full UI/retention policies not established.
No runtime execution of source or behavior scenarios.

R50.summary: Multi-user image hosting and share-gallery service with local/cloud storage routing; open-source and paid Core editions must be distinguished.
deployment: Self-hosted web server with separate frontend/backend
Docker Compose
JDK 1.8, MySQL 5.7+ and Redis
Separate Windows/macOS desktop clients usable with both editions
WeChat mini-program restricted to paid Core
R50.storage_model: Upload payloads go to local storage or a configured object/FTP backend; database records track ownership, names, storage source, quota and gallery membership. Current source also contains WebDAV upload/proxy support. Gallery entries associate image URLs/notes rather than requiring another original copy.
R50.privacy_model: Operator-managed server and storage, not E2EE. External object stores and configured moderation APIs may receive media; URL uploads cause server-side retrieval. Gallery password gates are application controls, not encryption assurances. README lists initial default admin credentials, which operators must replace.
maturity_notes: Frozen master commit 86987221123931366efbf79b9b029180ddcf52e4; latest open-source release 20240319 is dated 2024-03-19.
README explicitly calls repository code experimental and recommends supplied compiled packages rather than guaranteeing branch functionality.

Paid Core contains unspecified extra features; WeChat restriction is explicit despite the introductory all-platform marketing. Current branch WebDAV/chunk endpoints are not automatically attributed to the old release.
Official documentation URL could not be fetched because of a transport/DNS/TLS failure; primary README, release and substantial source inspected instead.
